reply: Her calm under pressure set her apart from the other candidates.
transferCue: Describe what makes your favourite café different.
transferReply: What sets it apart is the owner, who remembers everyone's order.
frame: Set someone apart from others / what sets it apart is…
nuance: Separable, usually with the object between: set her apart. Add from for the group: set apart from the rest. Often positive; a separate sense means reserve time or money.
contrast: Set apart makes something stand out; stand out is what the thing itself does.

exampleTranslations.Her calm under pressure set her apart fr: プレッシャーの中での落ち着きが、彼女を他の候補者から際立たせた。
exampleTranslations.What sets it apart is the owner, who rem: あの店を特別にしているのは、全員の注文を覚えている店主だ。

nuanceJapanese: 分離でき、たいてい目的語を間に置く：set her apart。比較対象は from で示す：set apart from the rest。多くは好意的な意味。別の意味で、時間やお金を取っておくこともある。
contrastJapanese: set apart は何かを際立たせること。stand out はそのもの自体が目立つこと。

meaning: Separate people or things that are together, or criticize something in detail.
easyEnglish: Separate people or things that are together, or criticize something in detail.
japanese: 引き離す。細かく批判する。
cue: Two children are fighting over a toy. Describe what you did.
reply: I had to pull them apart before someone got hurt.
transferCue: Describe how a reviewer treated your draft.
transferReply: She pulled the argument apart paragraph by paragraph, but her notes were fair.
frame: Pull people apart / pull an argument apart
nuance: Separable: pull them apart. With people it is physical separation; with a plan or piece of writing it means find every weakness. Tear apart is stronger and more emotional.
contrast: Pull apart separates or dissects; fall apart is what a thing does when it breaks by itself.

exampleTranslations.I had to pull them apart before someone: 誰かがけがをする前に、二人を引き離さなければならなかった。
exampleTranslations.She pulled the argument apart paragraph: 彼女は段落ごとに論旨を細かく崩していったが、指摘は公平だった。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：pull them apart。人なら物理的に引き離すこと、計画や文章ならあらゆる弱点を見つけること。tear apart はより強く感情的。
contrastJapanese: pull apart は引き離す、または細かく分析すること。fall apart は物が自然に壊れること。

meaning: Make or prepare something quickly and without much care.
easyEnglish: Make or prepare something quickly and without much care.
japanese: 手早く間に合わせで作る。
cue: Unexpected guests arrive at dinner time. Reassure your partner.
reply: I can throw together a pasta with what's in the fridge.
transferCue: Explain why a presentation looked rough.
transferReply: We threw it together the night before, so the slides don't match.
frame: Throw something together / throw a meal together
nuance: Separable: throw it together. Suggests speed and improvisation rather than poor quality. People can also be thrown together by circumstances: we were thrown together on a training course.
contrast: Throw together is fast and improvised; put together is careful assembly.

exampleTranslations.I can throw together a pasta with what's: 冷蔵庫にあるものでパスタをさっと作れるよ。
exampleTranslations.We threw it together the night before, s: 前の晩に急いでまとめたから、スライドの体裁がそろっていない。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：throw it together。速さと即興を表し、必ずしも質が低いわけではない。人が状況によって一緒になることも表す：we were thrown together on a training course。
contrastJapanese: throw together は手早い即興。put together は丁寧に組み立てること。

meaning: Join with other people in order to achieve something together.
easyEnglish: Join with other people in order to achieve something together.
japanese: 力を合わせるために団結する。
cue: Describe how your street dealt with a noisy construction site.
reply: The neighbours banded together and asked the council for quiet hours.
transferCue: Encourage colleagues to respond to a policy as a group.
transferReply: If we band together, they will have to listen. One complaint is easy to ignore.
frame: Band together / band together to do something / band together against something
nuance: No object. Usually a group with a shared problem or goal; add against for an opponent. Join forces means the same in more formal writing.
contrast: Band together is people uniting for a purpose; get together is simply meeting.

exampleTranslations.The neighbours banded together and asked: 近所の人たちが団結して、議会に静かな時間帯を設けるよう求めた。
exampleTranslations.If we band together, they will have to l: みんなで団結すれば、向こうも聞かざるを得ない。苦情ひとつなら無視されやすい。

nuanceJapanese: 目的語なし。共通の問題や目標を持つ集団が主語で、相手は against で示す。join forces はよりフォーマルな書き言葉で同じ意味。
contrastJapanese: band together は目的のために人が団結すること。get together は単に集まること。

meaning: Make fast progress or continue with determination.
easyEnglish: Make fast progress or continue with determination.
japanese: 力強く前進する。
cue: Give a short status update on a project that is going well.
reply: The design team is forging ahead. Two screens are already in testing.
transferCue: Describe a friend who kept studying while others quit.
transferReply: Most of the class dropped out, but she forged ahead and passed in June.
frame: Forge ahead / forge ahead with something
nuance: No object; add with for the project: forge ahead with the plan. Forge is pronounced with a soft g, like large. Slightly literary and positive.
contrast: Forge ahead stresses energetic progress; press ahead stresses continuing despite objections.

exampleTranslations.The design team is forging ahead. Two sc: デザインチームは順調に前進しています。すでに2画面がテストに入りました。
exampleTranslations.Most of the class dropped out, but she f: クラスの大半は脱落したけど、彼女は前に進み続けて6月に合格した。

nuanceJapanese: 目的語なし。対象は with で示す：forge ahead with the plan。forge の g は large と同じやわらかい音。やや文学的で前向きな表現。
contrastJapanese: forge ahead は力強い前進を強調する。press ahead は反対があっても続けることを強調する。

meaning: Move in front of others in a race, competition or market.
easyEnglish: Move in front of others in a race, competition or market.
japanese: 競争相手を抜いて先に出る。
cue: Describe how the sales race between two teams changed in March.
reply: Our team pulled ahead in March after the new pricing went live.
transferCue: Talk about a cycling race you watched.
transferReply: She pulled ahead on the final climb and won by twenty seconds.
frame: Pull ahead / pull ahead of someone
nuance: No object; add of for the rival: pull ahead of the competition. From racing, now common in business and sport. Get ahead is about personal success rather than a race.
contrast: Pull ahead overtakes a rival; get ahead advances in life or a career.

exampleTranslations.Our team pulled ahead in March after the: 新しい価格が始まった3月に、うちのチームが先に出た。
exampleTranslations.She pulled ahead on the final climb and: 彼女は最後の登りで抜け出し、20秒差で勝った。

nuanceJapanese: 目的語なし。相手は of で示す：pull ahead of the competition。レース由来で、今はビジネスやスポーツでよく使う。get ahead は競争ではなく個人の成功について。
contrastJapanese: pull ahead は競争相手を抜くこと。get ahead は人生や仕事で先に進むこと。

meaning: Continue moving or working towards a goal with effort.
easyEnglish: Continue moving or working towards a goal with effort.
japanese: 努力して前に進める。
cue: The first version of a feature got mixed feedback. Tell the team the plan.
reply: The feedback is useful, but we'll push forward with the release and fix the rough edges next sprint.
transferCue: Describe a hike in bad weather.
transferReply: The rain got heavier, but we pushed forward to the hut.
frame: Push forward / push forward with something
nuance: No object in this sense; add with for the plan. Push something forward can also mean move a date or item earlier or higher in priority. Push ahead and press ahead are close.
contrast: Push forward keeps moving despite effort; move on leaves one thing to start the next.

exampleTranslations.The feedback is useful, but we'll push f: フィードバックは役に立つけど、リリースは進めて、粗い部分は次のスプリントで直します。
exampleTranslations.The rain got heavier, but we pushed forw: 雨は強くなったが、私たちは山小屋まで進み続けた。

phrase: stick out like a sore thumb
meaning: Be very obviously different from everything around it.

meaning: Find a fair middle point between two things.

meaning: Make people feel that something is true for them.

meaning: Accept embarrassment in order to do the right thing.

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。つらさを認めたうえで促す表現なので、責める響きにならない。

meaning: Formally disagree with something said or written.
easyEnglish: Formally disagree with something said or written.
japanese: 異議を唱える。

reply: I take issue with the claim that this is settled.

nuanceJapanese: 異議の対象は with で示す。改まった正確な表現で、議論そのものに焦点を保てる。

meaning: Pause and think carefully about a situation.
easyEnglish: Pause and think carefully about a situation.
japanese: 立ち止まって、状況を見直す。

reply: Let's take stock before we plan the next one.

transferReply: I took stock and changed two things.

meaning: Make something unpleasant slightly less intense.

japanese: つらさや強さを、少しやわらげる。

transferReply: I had an apple to take the edge off my hunger.

nuanceJapanese: なくすのではなく弱める表現なので、部分的な軽減に合う。やわらげる対象は off で示す。

phrase: take the rough with the smooth
meaning: Accept the bad parts along with the good.
easyEnglish: Accept the bad parts along with the good.

frame: Take the rough with the smooth
nuance: British and fixed in form. It accepts a trade-off rather than complaining about it.

nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、形は固定。不満を述べるのではなく、差し引きを受け入れる表現。

meaning: Talk about work when you are not at work.
easyEnglish: Talk about work when you are not at work.

meaning: Do or say something that seems likely to bring bad luck.

meaning: Someone or something that almost everyone knows.

nuanceJapanese: 所有格はその人に合わせる。技能ではなく、すぐ使えることを表す。

meaning: Even if that is true, it does not change things.
easyEnglish: Even if that is true, it does not change things.
japanese: それはそうだとしても。
cue: Someone explains why a delay happened, but the deadline stands.
reply: Be that as it may, the client still needs it on Monday.
transferCue: Acknowledge a fair point before disagreeing.
transferReply: Be that as it may, I'd still rather not sign yet.
nuance: Formal and fixed, always at the start of a sentence. It concedes a point without accepting the conclusion.

exampleTranslations.Be that as it may, the client still need: それはそうだとしても、顧客は月曜に必要としています。
exampleTranslations.Be that as it may, I'd still rather not: それはそうだとしても、まだ署名はしたくありません。

nuanceJapanese: 改まった固定表現で、つねに文頭に置く。相手の指摘は認めつつ、結論には同意しないことを示す。

meaning: So extreme that it is hard to accept.
easyEnglish: So extreme that it is hard to accept.
japanese: 信じられないほどである。
cue: A service failure was worse than anything you had seen. React.
reply: The wait was beyond belief — four hours with no update.
transferCue: Describe an unexpectedly generous act.
transferReply: Their kindness that week was beyond belief.
nuance: Comes after the noun or be. It works for very bad and very good extremes.

exampleTranslations.The wait was beyond belief — four hours: 待ち時間は信じがたいほどでした。連絡もないまま4時間です。
exampleTranslations.Their kindness that week was beyond beli: あの週の彼らの親切は、信じられないほどでした。

nuanceJapanese: 名詞や be のあとに置く。極端に悪いことにも、極端によいことにも使える。

meaning: Stop yourself from saying what you think.
easyEnglish: Stop yourself from saying what you think.
japanese: 言いたいことをこらえる。
cue: You disagreed in a meeting but said nothing. Explain why.
reply: I bit my lip because the decision was already made.
transferCue: Advise a friend at a family gathering.
transferReply: You might have to bite your lip until the cake.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Similar to bite your tongue, which is slightly more common.

exampleTranslations.I bit my lip because the decision was al: もう決まったことだったので、言いたいことはこらえました。
exampleTranslations.You might have to bite your lip until th: ケーキが出るまでは、こらえておいたほうがいいかもしれません。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。bite your tongue とほぼ同じ意味で、そちらのほうがやや一般的。

meaning: Publicly disagree with your own group.
easyEnglish: Publicly disagree with your own group.
japanese: 味方であるはずの集団に、公然と異を唱える。
cue: One committee member disagreed publicly. Describe it.
reply: She broke ranks and said the timetable was unworkable.
transferCue: Describe a minister's unexpected statement.
transferReply: Two of them broke ranks over the funding cut.
nuance: Ranks is always plural. With introduces the group. It implies a visible, deliberate break.

exampleTranslations.She broke ranks and said the timetable w: 彼女は公然と異を唱え、日程は実行不可能だと述べました。
exampleTranslations.Two of them broke ranks over the funding: 資金削減をめぐり、2人が公然と異を唱えました。

nuanceJapanese: ranks はつねに複数形。集団は with で示す。目に見える、意図的な離反を含意する。

meaning: According to what everyone says.
easyEnglish: According to what everyone says.
japanese: 誰の話を聞いても。伝え聞くところでは。
cue: You did not attend an event but heard about it. Report it.
reply: By all accounts it was a good evening.
transferCue: Describe a new colleague you have not met.
transferReply: By all accounts she's very good with clients.
nuance: Usually opens a sentence. It marks second-hand information, which keeps you from overstating.

聞いたかぎりでは、よい夜だったようです。
exampleTranslations.By all accounts she's very good with cli: 誰に聞いても、彼女は顧客対応が上手だそうです。

nuanceJapanese: 文頭に置くことが多い。伝聞であることを示すので、断定を避けられる。

meaning: Certainly; please do.
easyEnglish: Certainly; please do.
japanese: ぜひどうぞ。もちろん構いません。
cue: Someone asks whether they may take a photograph.
reply: By all means. The light is better from that side.
transferCue: Agree to a colleague's request to join a call.
transferReply: By all means join us. I'll forward the invitation.
nuance: A polite, slightly formal yes. Means is always plural even in this fixed phrase.

exampleTranslations.By all means. The light is better from t: ぜひどうぞ。そちら側のほうが光がきれいです。
exampleTranslations.By all means join us. I'll forward the i: ぜひご参加ください。招待を転送します。

nuanceJapanese: 丁寧でやや改まった肯定の返事。この決まった形でも means はつねに複数形。

meaning: By a very large amount.
easyEnglish: By a very large amount.
japanese: はるかに。断然。
cue: One option is clearly better than the rest. Say so.
reply: This is by far the simplest of the three.
transferCue: Describe the busiest month of your year.
transferReply: March is by far our busiest month.
frame: By far the most / the best
nuance: Used with superlatives and comparatives. It usually comes before the.

exampleTranslations.This is by far the simplest of the three: 3つのなかで、これが断然いちばん簡単です。
3月は、断然いちばん忙しい月です。

nuanceJapanese: 最上級や比較級と一緒に使う。ふつうは the の前に置く。

meaning: Not at all.
easyEnglish: Not at all.
japanese: 決して〜ではない。
cue: Someone assumes a decision is final. Correct that impression.
reply: That's by no means settled. Two people still disagree.
transferCue: Qualify praise of your own work.
transferReply: It's by no means finished, but the structure is there.
nuance: A formal negative. At the start of a sentence it inverts the verb: by no means is it settled.

exampleTranslations.That's by no means settled. Two people s: 決して決まったわけではありません。まだ2人が反対しています。
exampleTranslations.It's by no means finished, but the struc: 完成には程遠いですが、骨組みはできています。

nuanceJapanese: 改まった否定表現。文頭に置くと倒置になり、by no means is it settled の形になる。

meaning: Make people doubt something.
easyEnglish: Make people doubt something.
japanese: 疑いを投げかける。信頼性を揺るがす。
cue: A new finding undermines an earlier report. Describe the effect.
reply: These results call into question the whole method.
transferCue: Describe how one error affected trust in a document.
transferReply: One wrong date can call into question everything else in it.
nuance: Formal. The object can sit between call and into, or after into question.

exampleTranslations.These results call into question the who: この結果は、手法全体の妥当性に疑いを投げかけます。
exampleTranslations.One wrong date can call into question ev: 日付ひとつの誤りが、そこに書かれたほかのすべてを疑わしくします。

nuanceJapanese: 改まった表現。目的語は call と into のあいだにも、into question のあとにも置ける。

meaning: Try to remember something from the past.
easyEnglish: Try to remember something from the past.
japanese: 過去のことを思い起こす。
cue: You want a colleague to recall an old meeting.
reply: Cast your mind back to the March review — who raised it?
transferCue: Introduce a memory in a speech.
transferReply: I cast my mind back to our first office above the bakery.
frame: Cast your mind back to something
nuance: To introduces the time or event. Slightly formal, and it invites rather than tests memory.

exampleTranslations.Cast your mind back to the March review: 3月の会議を思い出してください。あれを指摘したのは誰でしたか。
exampleTranslations.I cast my mind back to our first office: パン屋の上にあった最初の事務所を思い起こします。

nuanceJapanese: 時期や出来事は to で示す。やや改まった表現で、記憶を試すのではなく促す言い方。

meaning: Become known after being hidden.
easyEnglish: Become known after being hidden.
japanese: 隠れていたことが、明らかになる。
cue: An old problem surfaced during an audit. Report it neutrally.
reply: The discrepancy came to light during the audit.
transferCue: Describe how a family story emerged.
transferReply: The letters came to light when we cleared the attic.
nuance: The fact is the subject, not the person who found it. Neutral, so it avoids assigning blame.

exampleTranslations.The discrepancy came to light during the: その食い違いは、監査の過程で明らかになりました。
exampleTranslations.The letters came to light when we cleare: 屋根裏を片づけたときに、その手紙が出てきました。

nuanceJapanese: 主語は発見した人ではなく事実のほう。中立的なので、責任の所在を示さずに済む。

meaning: End without any result.
easyEnglish: End without any result.
japanese: 結局、何にもならずに終わる。
cue: A long negotiation produced no agreement. Summarise.
reply: Six months of talks came to nothing.
transferCue: Describe a hopeful lead that faded.
transferReply: The introduction came to nothing, but I learned a lot.
nuance: The effort is the subject. It reports a result without blaming anyone.

半年にわたる協議は、結局何にもなりませんでした。
exampleTranslations.The introduction came to nothing, but I: あの紹介は実を結びませんでしたが、学ぶことは多かったです。

nuanceJapanese: 主語は取り組みのほう。誰も責めずに結果だけを述べる表現。

meaning: Whatever happens.
easyEnglish: Whatever happens.
japanese: 何が起ころうとも。
cue: A friend worries you might cancel again. Reassure them.
reply: I'll be there on Saturday, come what may.
transferCue: Commit to finishing something difficult.
transferReply: Come what may, we're submitting on the thirtieth.
nuance: Fixed and slightly literary. It sits at the start or end of a sentence, set off by a comma.

exampleTranslations.I'll be there on Saturday, come what may: 何があっても、土曜には行きます。
exampleTranslations.Come what may, we're submitting on the t: 何があろうと、30日には提出します。

nuanceJapanese: 形が固定した、やや文語的な表現。文頭か文末に置き、コンマで区切る。

meaning: Something that everyone in a group already knows.
easyEnglish: Something that everyone in a group already knows.
japanese: みんなが知っている、周知の事実。
cue: Someone worries about sharing a fact that is already public.
reply: It's common knowledge by now. It was in the newsletter.
transferCue: Correct an assumption that a fact was secret.
transferReply: I thought it was common knowledge that she'd moved teams.
nuance: Uncountable, so no article. It refers to a specific group, so say who if it matters.

exampleTranslations.It's common knowledge by now. It was in: もう周知のことです。会報にも載っていました。
exampleTranslations.I thought it was common knowledge that s: 彼女のチーム異動は、みんな知っていることだと思っていました。

nuanceJapanese: 不可算名詞なので冠詞は付かない。特定の集団の中での話なので、必要なら範囲を添える。

meaning: Hope that something goes well.
easyEnglish: Hope that something goes well.
japanese: うまくいくように願う。
cue: A friend is waiting on a decision tomorrow. Wish them luck.
reply: I'll cross my fingers for you tomorrow.
transferCue: Describe waiting for a delayed train connection.
transferReply: We crossed our fingers and made the last connection.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject and fingers is plural. Keep your fingers crossed is equally common.

明日、うまくいくよう祈っています。
exampleTranslations.We crossed our fingers and made the last: 祈るような気持ちで、最後の乗り継ぎに間に合いました。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせ、fingers は複数形。keep your fingers crossed も同じくらいよく使う。

meaning: Get your first experience of a kind of work.
easyEnglish: Get your first experience of a kind of work.
japanese: その分野での経験を、最初に積む。
cue: A colleague asks where you learned to handle difficult clients.
reply: I cut my teeth on complaints at a call centre.
transferCue: Describe where a well-known figure started.
transferReply: She cut her teeth on local radio before television.
nuance: On introduces the early work, and the possessive follows the subject. It implies formative experience.

exampleTranslations.I cut my teeth on complaints at a call c: コールセンターの苦情対応で、最初の経験を積みました。
exampleTranslations.She cut her teeth on local radio before: 彼女はテレビの前に、地方ラジオで経験を積みました。

nuanceJapanese: 最初の仕事は on で示し、所有格は主語に合わせる。基礎を作った経験という含みがある。

meaning: Extremely tired.
easyEnglish: Extremely tired.
japanese: 立っていられないほど疲れている。
cue: A colleague has worked two long shifts. Send them home.
reply: You're dead on your feet. Go home and finish tomorrow.
transferCue: Describe how you felt after a long day of travel.
transferReply: By the time we checked in I was dead on my feet.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Informal and hyperbolic; it is about tiredness only.

exampleTranslations.You're dead on your feet. Go home and fi: もうへとへとですね。帰って明日にしましょう。
exampleTranslations.By the time we checked in I was dead on: チェックインする頃には、もう立っているのがやっとでした。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。くだけた大げさな言い方で、疲労だけを指す。

meaning: Perform a small ceremonial task for a group.
easyEnglish: Perform a small ceremonial task for a group.
japanese: その場の役目を、代表して務める。
cue: A cake needs cutting at a small party. Invite someone.
reply: Would you do the honours and cut the first slice?
transferCue: Ask someone to pour the drinks.
transferReply: You brought it, so you should do the honours.
nuance: Honours is always plural; American English spells it honors. Light and slightly ceremonious.

exampleTranslations.Would you do the honours and cut the fir: 最初のひと切れを、切ってくださいませんか。
exampleTranslations.You brought it, so you should do the hon: 持ってきてくれたのはあなたなので、注ぐ役もお願いします。

nuanceJapanese: honours はつねに複数形で、アメリカ英語では honors とつづる。軽く儀礼的な響き。

meaning: At some point in the future.
easyEnglish: At some point in the future.
japanese: この先、いずれ。
cue: A decision can wait but will matter later. Note it.
reply: We'll need a bigger server down the line, not this year.
transferCue: Describe a consequence of a choice made now.
transferReply: Choosing the cheaper option costs more down the line.
nuance: American English often says down the road. Often with further or somewhere for vagueness.

exampleTranslations.We'll need a bigger server down the line: 今年ではありませんが、いずれ大きなサーバーが必要になります。
exampleTranslations.Choosing the cheaper option costs more d: 安いほうを選ぶと、いずれ費用がかさみます。

nuanceJapanese: アメリカ英語では down the road と言うことが多い。further や somewhere を添えて、時期をぼかすこともある。

meaning: Be the one given the least pleasant task.
easyEnglish: Be the one given the least pleasant task.
japanese: いちばん嫌な役回りを引き当てる。
cue: Someone has to work on a public holiday. Describe who.
reply: I drew the short straw and I'm covering the holiday.
transferCue: Describe how a family decided who drives.
transferReply: My brother drew the short straw and drove both ways.
nuance: Straw is singular and takes the. It implies chance rather than an unfair decision.

exampleTranslations.I drew the short straw and I'm covering: 貧乏くじを引いて、祝日の当番は私になりました。
exampleTranslations.My brother drew the short straw and drov: 兄が貧乏くじを引いて、往復とも運転しました。

nuanceJapanese: straw は単数で the を伴う。不当な決定ではなく、運の結果という含みがある。

meaning: Stop being careful and become vulnerable.
easyEnglish: Stop being careful and become vulnerable.
japanese: 警戒をゆるめて、隙を見せる。
cue: A careful process failed in the final week. Explain how.
reply: We dropped our guard in the last week and missed the check.
transferCue: Describe becoming comfortable with new people.
transferReply: It took a month before I dropped my guard with them.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Negative about carelessness, positive about trusting people.

exampleTranslations.We dropped our guard in the last week an: 最後の週に気をゆるめて、確認を飛ばしてしまいました。
exampleTranslations.It took a month before I dropped my guar: 彼らに対して気を許すまでに、1か月かかりました。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。不注意について使えば否定的、人に心を開く意味では肯定的になる。

meaning: That is reasonable; I accept it.
easyEnglish: That is reasonable; I accept it.
japanese: なるほど、もっともだ。
cue: A friend explains why they cannot come. Accept it warmly.
reply: Fair enough. Let's find another weekend.
transferCue: Accept a colleague's objection to a deadline.
transferReply: Fair enough — let's move it to Wednesday.
nuance: Informal, usually a full response on its own. It accepts a reason without necessarily agreeing.

なるほど、分かりました。別の週末を探しましょう。
exampleTranslations.Fair enough — let's move it to Wednesday: もっともですね。水曜に動かしましょう。

nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現で、それだけで返答になる。同意までは示さず、理由を受け入れることを表す。

meaning: Something people may reasonably criticise or pursue.
easyEnglish: Something people may reasonably criticise or pursue.
japanese: 批判や追及の対象にされても仕方がないもの。
cue: A public figure's policy is criticised, but their family is not. Draw the line.
reply: Her policies are fair game; her children are not.
transferCue: Describe what a review may cover.
transferReply: Anything we published is fair game for the review.
nuance: Uncountable, so no article. It marks something as legitimately open to criticism.

exampleTranslations.Her policies are fair game; her children: 彼女の政策は批判されて当然ですが、子どもは別です。
exampleTranslations.Anything we published is fair game for t: 公開したものはすべて、検証の対象になって当然です。

nuanceJapanese: 不可算名詞なので冠詞は付かない。批判の対象として正当だと示す表現。

meaning: Look for and point out problems in something.
easyEnglish: Look for and point out problems in something.
japanese: あら探しをして、欠点を指摘する。
cue: A colleague criticises every version of a document. Describe it.
reply: He finds fault with every draft but never suggests wording.
transferCue: Describe how you try to give feedback.
transferReply: I try not to find fault with the parts that are working.
nuance: With introduces the target. Fault stays singular, and the phrase is usually critical of the critic.

exampleTranslations.He finds fault with every draft but neve: 彼はどの草稿にも欠点を指摘しますが、代案の表現は出しません。
exampleTranslations.I try not to find fault with the parts t: うまくいっている部分については、あら探しをしないようにしています。

nuanceJapanese: 対象は with で示す。fault は単数のままで、批判する側への否定的な評価を含むことが多い。

meaning: Most importantly, before anything else.
easyEnglish: Most importantly, before anything else.
japanese: 何よりもまず。
cue: You are explaining your priority in a short speech.
reply: First and foremost, thank you for staying late this week.
transferCue: Describe how you see your own role.
transferReply: First and foremost I'm a teacher, and the admin comes second.
nuance: Opens a sentence, followed by a comma. Slightly formal, and stronger than simply first.

exampleTranslations.First and foremost, thank you for stayin: 何よりもまず、今週遅くまで残ってくれてありがとうございます。
exampleTranslations.First and foremost I'm a teacher, and th: 私はまず教師であり、事務はそのあとです。

nuanceJapanese: 文頭に置いてコンマを続ける。やや改まった表現で、単なる first より強い。

meaning: In every practical sense, if not officially.
easyEnglish: In every practical sense, if not officially.
japanese: 実質的には。事実上。
cue: A colleague acts as team lead without the title. Describe the situation.
reply: For all intents and purposes she already runs the team.
transferCue: Describe a project that is finished apart from paperwork.
transferReply: For all intents and purposes it's done. Only signatures remain.
nuance: Formal and fixed; it is not for all intensive purposes. It contrasts practice with formal status.

exampleTranslations.For all intents and purposes she already: 実質的には、彼女がすでにチームを率いています。
実質的には完了しています。あとは署名だけです。

nuanceJapanese: 改まった固定表現で、for all intensive purposes は誤り。実態と公式な扱いを対比させる。

meaning: Whether the result is good or bad.
easyEnglish: Whether the result is good or bad.
japanese: よかれあしかれ。
cue: A decision has already been made and cannot change. Accept it.
reply: For better or worse, we've chosen the new system.
transferCue: Describe a change in your neighbourhood.
transferReply: For better or worse, the whole street has changed.
nuance: Usually opens a sentence. It accepts uncertainty about the outcome rather than predicting it.

exampleTranslations.For better or worse, we've chosen the ne: よかれあしかれ、新しい仕組みを選びました。
exampleTranslations.For better or worse, the whole street ha: よかれあしかれ、通り全体が変わりました。

nuanceJapanese: 文頭に置くのがふつう。結果を予測するのではなく、不確かさを受け入れる表現。

meaning: Mostly, though not entirely.
easyEnglish: Mostly, though not entirely.
japanese: おおむね。大部分は。
cue: A process works well with occasional problems. Summarise it.
reply: For the most part it runs itself, apart from Mondays.
transferCue: Describe your experience of a long course.
transferReply: For the most part the teaching was excellent.
nuance: Opens a sentence or follows the verb. It leaves room for exceptions, so it reads as honest.

exampleTranslations.For the most part it runs itself, apart: 月曜を除けば、おおむね自動で回っています。
exampleTranslations.For the most part the teaching was excel: おおむね、教え方は素晴らしかったです。

nuanceJapanese: 文頭か動詞のあとに置く。例外の余地を残すので、率直な印象になる。

meaning: Do something harmful to someone because they harmed you.
easyEnglish: Do something harmful to someone because they harmed you.
japanese: 仕返しをして、貸し借りをなしにする。
cue: A friend wants revenge for an unfair review. Advise against it.
reply: Trying to get even will cost you more than it costs them.
transferCue: Describe a rivalry that ended well.
transferReply: They stopped trying to get even and started sharing customers.
nuance: With introduces the person. Informal, and usually the thing being advised against.

exampleTranslations.Trying to get even will cost you more th: 仕返しをしても、相手より自分のほうが失うものが大きいですよ。
exampleTranslations.They stopped trying to get even and star: 彼らは仕返しをやめて、顧客を共有し始めました。

nuanceJapanese: 相手は with で示す。くだけた表現で、たいていは勧められない行動として語られる。

meaning: Make no progress at all.
easyEnglish: Make no progress at all.
japanese: まったく進展しない。
cue: Three calls to support produced nothing. Report it.
reply: I've called twice and got nowhere.
transferCue: Describe an argument that went in circles.
transferReply: We argued for an hour and got nowhere.
nuance: With introduces the task or person. Get nowhere fast adds emphasis, not speed.

2回電話しましたが、まったく進展しません。
1時間議論して、まったく前に進みませんでした。

nuanceJapanese: 対象や相手は with で示す。get nowhere fast は速さではなく、強調を加える言い方。

phrase: get on like a house on fire
meaning: Like each other immediately and very much.
easyEnglish: Like each other immediately and very much.
japanese: すぐに意気投合して、とても仲よくなる。
cue: Two friends you introduced became close at once. Describe it.
reply: They got on like a house on fire from the first evening.
transferCue: Describe meeting a colleague's family.
transferReply: My mother and his sister get on like a house on fire.
frame: Get on like a house on fire
nuance: British; American English says get along. Warm and positive despite the alarming image.

exampleTranslations.They got on like a house on fire from th: 二人は最初の晩から、すっかり意気投合していました。
exampleTranslations.My mother and his sister get on like a h: 母と彼の妹は、とても気が合っています。

nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、アメリカ英語では get along と言う。物騒な比喩だが、温かく肯定的な表現。
pronunciation: ɡet ɑːn laɪk ə haʊs ɑːn ˈfaɪɚ

meaning: Approximately, allowing a small difference.
easyEnglish: Approximately, allowing a small difference.
japanese: 多少の誤差はあるとして、おおよそ。
cue: A friend asks how long the journey takes.
reply: About two hours, give or take twenty minutes.
transferCue: Estimate how many people attended an event.

nuanceJapanese: 数字のあとに、ふつうはコンマを置いて続ける。誤差の幅は言っても言わなくてもよい。

meaning: Accidentally reveal a secret.
easyEnglish: Accidentally reveal a secret.
japanese: うっかり秘密を明かしてしまう。

nuanceJapanese: 主語は人でも、表情などの兆候でもよい。意図的に話すのではなく、うっかり漏れることを指す。

meaning: Treat someone gently, or use less of something.

meaning: Share the cost of something equally.

reply: Shall we go halves on the present?
transferCue: Describe how two housemates bought a shared item.
transferReply: We went halves on the washing machine.

meaning: Explain something thoroughly.

transferReply: I'd rather not go into detail, but it's being handled.

exampleTranslations.I won't go into detail now, but I'll wri: 今は詳しく触れませんが、午後に書いてお送りします。
exampleTranslations.I'd rather not go into detail, but it's: 詳しくは触れたくありませんが、対応は進んでいます。

nuanceJapanese: detail はふつう単数。否定形で使うことが非常に多く、話を短く切り上げる丁寧な言い方になる。

meaning: Do something by yourself instead of with others.
easyEnglish: Do something by yourself instead of with others.
japanese: 人と組まず、単独でやる。
cue: A colleague is considering leaving to start a business. Reflect it back.
reply: So you're thinking of going it alone after five years here?
transferCue: Describe a musician leaving a band.
transferReply: She went it alone and released the album herself.
nuance: Fixed with it, which has no reference. Neutral to admiring about independence.

exampleTranslations.So you're thinking of going it alone aft: ここで5年働いたあと、独立を考えているということですね。
exampleTranslations.She went it alone and released the album: 彼女は単独で動き、自らアルバムを出しました。

meaning: Keep discussing something without making progress.
easyEnglish: Keep discussing something without making progress.
japanese: 堂々巡りで、話が先に進まない。
cue: A meeting keeps returning to the same point. Interrupt usefully.
reply: We're going round in circles. Shall we vote?
transferCue: Describe a decision you could not make alone.
transferReply: I went round in circles for a week before asking for advice.

exampleTranslations.We're going round in circles. Shall we v: 堂々巡りになっています。採決しませんか。

nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語では round、アメリカ英語では around。circles はつねに複数形。

meaning: Be destroyed or come to nothing.
easyEnglish: Be destroyed or come to nothing.
japanese: すべて台なしになる。

reply: Six months of planning went up in smoke in one email.
transferCue: Describe a savings plan hit by an emergency.
transferReply: The deposit went up in smoke when the boiler failed.

nuanceJapanese: 主語は計画やお金のほう。大げさな表現で、突然すべてを失う含みがある。

meaning: Working very closely together.
easyEnglish: Working very closely together.
japanese: ぴったりと連携して。

reply: Design and support worked hand in glove on this release.
transferCue: Describe two organisations with a close arrangement.
transferReply: The two charities operate hand in glove.
frame: Work hand in glove with someone
nuance: No articles inside the phrase. It can hint at collusion, so tone matters.

nuanceJapanese: 句の中に冠詞は入らない。共謀をほのめかすこともあるので、口調に注意する。

meaning: Fixed and not open to exceptions.
easyEnglish: Fixed and not open to exceptions.
japanese: 例外を認めない、厳格な。

reply: There's no hard and fast rule. Use your judgement.

transferReply: The safety check is a hard and fast rule.
nuance: Almost always before rule or rules, and very often negative: no hard and fast rule.

exampleTranslations.The safety check is a hard and fast rule: 安全確認だけは、例外のない決まりです。

nuanceJapanese: ほぼつねに rule の前に置き、no hard and fast rule の否定形で使うことが非常に多い。

meaning: Enjoy an opportunity to do something, often at others' expense.
easyEnglish: Enjoy an opportunity to do something, often at others' expense.
japanese: ここぞとばかりに、思う存分やる。
cue: A public mistake will attract heavy commentary. Predict the reaction.
reply: The press will have a field day with this.
transferCue: Describe children in a new playground.
transferReply: The kids had a field day on the climbing frame.
frame: Have a field day with something
nuance: With introduces the material. Often about critics enjoying someone's difficulty, but it can be innocent.

exampleTranslations.The press will have a field day with thi: 報道はここぞとばかりに書き立てるでしょう。
exampleTranslations.The kids had a field day on the climbing: 子どもたちは、ジャングルジムで思いきり遊びました。

meaning: Have a personal interest in how something turns out.
easyEnglish: Have a personal interest in how something turns out.
japanese: 結果に自分の利害が関わっている。
cue: Explain why a department should be consulted.
reply: They have a stake in this, so they should see the draft.
transferCue: Describe why residents joined a planning meeting.
transferReply: Everyone on the street has a stake in the decision.
nuance: In introduces the matter. It can mean financial ownership or simply a personal interest.

exampleTranslations.They have a stake in this, so they shoul: この件は彼らの利害に関わるので、草案を見てもらうべきです。

nuanceJapanese: 対象は in で示す。金銭的な持ち分にも、単に個人的な利害にも使う。

meaning: Want to cause trouble for someone because you dislike them.
easyEnglish: Want to cause trouble for someone because you dislike them.
japanese: 目の敵にして、つらく当たる。

reply: You feel like she has it in for you, is that right?
transferCue: Reassure someone who suspects unfair treatment.
transferReply: I don't think anyone has it in for you. The rota is random.
nuance: For introduces the target. A serious accusation, so it is often softened with I think or it feels like.

nuanceJapanese: 対象は for で示す。重い指摘なので、I think や it feels like を添えてやわらげることが多い。

meaning: Reduce risk by not committing to one option.
easyEnglish: Reduce risk by not committing to one option.
japanese: ひとつに賭けず、危険を分散する。
cue: A colleague has applied to two very different programmes. Describe it.

transferReply: I hedged my bets and paid extra for the flexible fare.

exampleTranslations.I hedged my bets and paid extra for the: 念のため、追加料金を払って変更可能な運賃にしました。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせ、bets は複数形。中立から、優柔不断への軽い批判まで幅がある。

meaning: Have great and often sudden success or luck.
easyEnglish: Have great and often sudden success or luck.
japanese: 大当たりを引く。

reply: You hit the jackpot with that one.

transferReply: We hit the jackpot when she applied.

彼女が応募してくれたのは、大当たりでした。

transferReply: Her theory holds water even with the new data.

nuanceJapanese: 主語は主張や説明のほう。water に冠詞は付かず、否定形で使うことが最も多い。

meaning: Perform as well as the others around you.
easyEnglish: Perform as well as the others around you.

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせ、比較対象は against で示す。互角に戦えたことを控えめにほめる表現。

meaning: In a difficult situation that is hard to escape.
easyEnglish: In a difficult situation that is hard to escape.

nuanceJapanese: くだけたイギリス英語で、アメリカ英語では in a bind と言う。失敗ではなく、状況の難しさを表す。

meaning: In practice, whatever the formal position is.
easyEnglish: In practice, whatever the formal position is.

nuance: A double negative meaning very clearly. Terms is always plural, and it usually follows a verb of speaking.

nuanceJapanese: 二重否定で「きわめて明確に」の意味になる。terms はつねに複数形で、発言を表す動詞のあとに置く。

meaning: Involved in something too difficult for you.

meaning: Despite having to deal with something difficult.
easyEnglish: Despite having to deal with something difficult.
japanese: 困難に直面しながらも。

exampleTranslations.They finished in the face of real diffic: 本当に厳しい状況のなかで、彼らはやり遂げました。

meaning: Following something, usually as a result of it.
easyEnglish: Following something, usually as a result of it.

exampleTranslations.You alluded to a risk earlier. Could you: 先ほど危険をほのめかしていましたが、具体的に教えていただけますか。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない、やや改まった表現。つねに間接的な言及を指し、直接的にもなる refer to とは異なる。
contrastJapanese: allude to はほのめかす。refer to は直接名指しする。

meaning: Take responsibility for something and explain it.
easyEnglish: Take responsibility for something and explain it.
japanese: 責任を負って、説明する立場に立つ。
cue: A decision will need explaining at a review. Say who will do it.
reply: I'll answer for the delay. It was my call.
transferCue: Describe accountability in a team.
transferReply: Each lead answers for their own budget.
nuance: Inseparable. Have a lot to answer for is a common critical variant.
contrast: Answer for takes responsibility; account for explains a cause or a total.

exampleTranslations.I'll answer for the delay. It was my cal: 遅延については私が説明します。私の判断でした。
各責任者が、自分の予算について説明責任を負います。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。have a lot to answer for は、批判を込めたよくある言い方。
contrastJapanese: answer for は責任を負う。account for は原因や内訳を説明する。

meaning: Have a strong wish to achieve something.
easyEnglish: Have a strong wish to achieve something.
japanese: ある目標を、強く目指す。
cue: A colleague asks where you want to be in five years.
reply: I aspire to run a team of my own eventually.
transferCue: Describe what a small organisation wants to become.
transferReply: They aspire to the same standard as the national museums.
frame: Aspire to something / to do something
nuance: Inseparable and formal. Followed by a noun or by to plus a verb.
contrast: Aspire to is a long-term ambition; aim for is about a specific target.

exampleTranslations.I aspire to run a team of my own eventua: いずれは自分のチームを率いたいと思っています。
exampleTranslations.They aspire to the same standard as the: 彼らは、国立の博物館と同じ水準を目指しています。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない改まった表現。名詞か、to＋動詞を続ける。
contrastJapanese: aspire to は長期的な志。aim for は具体的な目標に向けること。

meaning: Deal with something that needs your attention.
easyEnglish: Deal with something that needs your attention.
japanese: 必要なことに、きちんと対応する。
cue: A customer is waiting while you finish a task.
reply: I'll attend to that as soon as I've finished here.
transferCue: Explain a short absence from a meeting.
transferReply: I had to attend to something at home for ten minutes.
nuance: Inseparable and slightly formal. Attend a meeting has no to and means be present.
contrast: Attend to deals with something; see to arranges for it to be done.

exampleTranslations.I'll attend to that as soon as I've fini: こちらが終わり次第、すぐに対応します。
exampleTranslations.I had to attend to something at home for: 家の用事で、10分ほど席を外していました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない、やや改まった表現。attend a meeting には to が付かず、「出席する」の意味になる。
contrastJapanese: attend to は自分で対応する。see to は手配して済ませる。

meaning: Result in a particular average over time.
easyEnglish: Result in a particular average over time.
japanese: ならしてみると、ある平均になる。
cue: Weekly figures vary a lot. Describe the overall picture.
reply: It averages out at about forty a week.
transferCue: Describe uneven costs across a year.
transferReply: The bills average out to roughly the same each month.
frame: Average out at / to a figure
nuance: Separable with an object: average them out. At or to introduces the figure.
contrast: Average out gives a mean over time; add up gives a total.

ならすと、週におよそ40件になります。
exampleTranslations.The bills average out to roughly the sam: 請求額は、ならせば毎月ほぼ同じくらいになります。

nuanceJapanese: 目的語を挟める：average them out。平均の値は at か to で示す。
contrastJapanese: average out は期間全体の平均を出す。add up は合計を出す。

meaning: Have its back facing something.
easyEnglish: Have its back facing something.
japanese: 裏手が〜に面している。
cue: A friend asks what the garden looks onto.
reply: The house backs onto a park, so it's very quiet.
transferCue: Describe a flat you are considering.
transferReply: It backs onto the railway, which is the only drawback.
nuance: Inseparable, with the building as subject. American English often says back up to.
contrast: Back onto describes the rear; look onto describes the view from the front.

exampleTranslations.The house backs onto a park, so it's ver: 家の裏手が公園なので、とても静かです。
exampleTranslations.It backs onto the railway, which is the: 裏手が線路で、そこだけが難点です。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、建物のほうが主語になる。アメリカ英語では back up to と言うことが多い。
contrastJapanese: back onto は裏手の向き。look onto は正面からの眺め。

meaning: Move threateningly towards someone, or press hard on something.
easyEnglish: Move threateningly towards someone, or press hard on something.
japanese: 迫ってくる。強く圧力をかける。
cue: A deadline is approaching fast. Describe the pressure.
reply: The deadline is bearing down on us now.
transferCue: Describe a storm approaching a coast.
transferReply: The weather front was bearing down on the island by evening.
nuance: Inseparable. Bear is irregular: bore, borne. It suggests threat or weight, not gentle approach.
contrast: Bear down on approaches with pressure; close in on surrounds and narrows.

締め切りが、いよいよ迫ってきています。
exampleTranslations.The weather front was bearing down on th: 夕方には、前線が島に迫っていました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。bear は不規則変化で bore、borne。穏やかな接近ではなく、圧迫感を伴う。
contrastJapanese: bear down on は圧迫しながら迫る。close in on は包囲して狭める。

meaning: Show that something is true.
easyEnglish: Show that something is true.
japanese: 正しいことを裏づける。
cue: New data supports an earlier claim. Report it.
reply: The results bear out what she predicted in March.
transferCue: Describe evidence that supported your account.
transferReply: The photographs bore me out.
nuance: Separable: bear it out, bear me out. The evidence is the subject, not the person.
contrast: Bear out confirms a claim; back up supports it with evidence you provide.

exampleTranslations.The results bear out what she predicted: その結果は、彼女が3月に予測したことを裏づけています。
写真が、私の話を裏づけてくれました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：bear it out、bear me out。主語は人ではなく証拠のほう。
contrastJapanese: bear out は主張が正しいと示す。back up は自分で根拠を添えて支える。

meaning: Cope with a difficult situation.
easyEnglish: Cope with a difficult situation.
japanese: つらい状況のなかで、なんとか持ちこたえる。
cue: A friend asks how someone is coping after a loss.
reply: She's bearing up, though it's early days.
transferCue: Answer honestly when asked how you are during a hard month.
transferReply: I'm bearing up, thanks for asking.
nuance: Intransitive. Gentle and understated, often used when someone does not want to say more.
contrast: Bear up is quiet endurance; hold up asks whether something is still working.

exampleTranslations.She's bearing up, though it's early days: まだ日が浅いですが、彼女はなんとか持ちこたえています。
なんとかやっています。気にかけてくれてありがとう。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。控えめでやわらかい言い方で、多くを語りたくないときにも使う。
contrastJapanese: bear up は静かに耐えること。hold up は持ちこたえているかを問う。

meaning: Work hard and steadily at something.
easyEnglish: Work hard and steadily at something.
japanese: こつこつと働き続ける。
cue: A colleague has been quietly productive all week. Describe it.
reply: He's been beavering away at the index since Monday.
transferCue: Describe your weekend project.
transferReply: I beavered away at the shed all Sunday.
nuance: Intransitive, informal and British. At introduces the task.
contrast: Beaver away is steady quiet work; slog away emphasises how hard it feels.

exampleTranslations.He's been beavering away at the index si: 彼は月曜から、索引作りにこつこつ取り組んでいます。
日曜は一日中、物置の作業をこつこつ進めました。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、くだけたイギリス英語。作業の対象は at で示す。
contrastJapanese: beaver away は黙々と着実に。slog away はつらさを強調する。

meaning: Sing or play something very loudly.
easyEnglish: Sing or play something very loudly.
japanese: 大声で歌う。大音量で演奏する。
cue: Describe a friend's driving habits.
reply: He belts out the chorus every single time.
transferCue: Describe a school concert.
transferReply: Thirty children belted out the final song.
nuance: Separable: belt it out. Informal and always about volume rather than quality.
contrast: Belt out is loud singing; drown out makes another sound impossible to hear.

exampleTranslations.He belts out the chorus every single tim: 彼は毎回、サビを大声で歌います。
exampleTranslations.Thirty children belted out the final son: 30人の子どもたちが、最後の歌を声を張って歌いました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：belt it out。くだけた表現で、質ではなく音量についての言い方。
contrastJapanese: belt out は大声で歌うこと。drown out は別の音をかき消すこと。

meaning: Suddenly be unable to remember anything.
easyEnglish: Suddenly be unable to remember anything.
japanese: 頭が真っ白になって、思い出せなくなる。
cue: You forgot your lines during a presentation. Describe it.
reply: I blanked out completely for about five seconds.
transferCue: Describe a moment in an exam.
transferReply: I blanked out on the first question and came back to it.
nuance: Intransitive in this sense. Blank something out instead means hide or erase it.
contrast: Blank out is a sudden memory gap; zone out is drifting inattention.

exampleTranslations.I blanked out completely for about five: 5秒ほど、完全に頭が真っ白になりました。
exampleTranslations.I blanked out on the first question and: 最初の問題で頭が真っ白になり、あとから戻りました。

nuanceJapanese: この意味では自動詞。blank something out なら「消す・隠す」という別の意味になる。
contrastJapanese: blank out は突然記憶が飛ぶこと。zone out はぼんやり上の空になること。

meaning: Close a route or reserve a period of time.
easyEnglish: Close a route or reserve a period of time.
japanese: 通れなくする。時間を確保して空けておく。
cue: You need uninterrupted time this week. Explain your plan.
reply: I've blocked off Thursday morning for the report.
transferCue: Describe a closed road during works.
transferReply: They blocked off the whole street for two days.
nuance: Separable: block it off. Used for both physical routes and time in a calendar.
contrast: Block off reserves or closes; cordon off puts a barrier around an area.

exampleTranslations.I've blocked off Thursday morning for th: 報告書のために、木曜の午前を空けてあります。
exampleTranslations.They blocked off the whole street for tw: 工事で、通り全体が2日間封鎖されました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：block it off。道路などの物理的な封鎖にも、予定表の時間確保にも使う。
contrastJapanese: block off は封鎖や確保。cordon off は区域の周囲に規制線を張ること。

meaning: Say something suddenly without thinking.
easyEnglish: Say something suddenly without thinking.
japanese: 思わず口走ってしまう。
cue: You accidentally revealed a surprise. Confess.
reply: I blurted out the whole plan before I could stop myself.

transferReply: She blurted out exactly what everyone was thinking.
nuance: Separable: blurt it out. It always implies speaking before thinking.
contrast: Blurt out is unplanned speech; spit it out urges someone to speak at last.

exampleTranslations.I blurted out the whole plan before I co: 止める間もなく、計画をすっかり口走ってしまいました。
exampleTranslations.She blurted out exactly what everyone wa: 彼女は、みんなが思っていたことをそのまま口にしました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：blurt it out。つねに、考える前に口に出すという含みがある。
contrastJapanese: blurt out は思わず口に出すこと。spit it out は早く言えと促す表現。

meaning: Become uncontrolled, especially anger.
easyEnglish: Become uncontrolled, especially anger.
japanese: 感情が抑えきれずにあふれ出す。

contrast: Boil over is a build-up that overflows; blow up is a sudden explosion of anger.

exampleTranslations.The frustration boiled over at the end o: 会議の終わりに、たまっていた不満が噴き出しました。
exampleTranslations.Tempers boiled over after the second boo: 2枚目の警告のあと、感情が一気に噴き出しました。

contrastJapanese: boil over は積もったものがあふれること。blow up は突然の怒りの爆発。

meaning: Be very close to a particular quality or state.
easyEnglish: Be very close to a particular quality or state.

transferReply: His interest in trains borders on obsession.
nuance: Inseparable, followed by a noun or -ing. It softens a strong judgement into a near one.
contrast: Border on is almost being something; verge on is a near-identical alternative.

exampleTranslations.The delay bordered on rude, though I'm s: あの遅さはほとんど失礼と言えるほどでしたが、悪気はなかったはずです。
exampleTranslations.His interest in trains borders on obsess: 彼の鉄道への関心は、ほとんど執着と言えるほどです。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、名詞か -ing を続ける。強い断定を「ほぼそうだ」とやわらげられる。
contrastJapanese: border on は「ほとんどそうだ」。verge on もほぼ同じ意味で使える。

meaning: Test an idea by describing it to someone.
easyEnglish: Test an idea by describing it to someone.
japanese: 考えを人にぶつけて、反応を見る。

transferReply: I bounce drafts off my sister before sending them.

contrast: Bounce off seeks a quick reaction; run by asks for approval or a check.

exampleTranslations.Can I bounce an idea off you for two min: 2分だけ、考えを聞かせてもらってもいいですか。
exampleTranslations.I bounce drafts off my sister before sen: 送る前に、草稿を姉に見てもらって反応を聞きます。

contrastJapanese: bounce off は反応を見る。run by は確認や了承を求める。

meaning: Surprise and delight someone very much.
easyEnglish: Surprise and delight someone very much.
japanese: 驚くほど感激させる。

reply: The welcome completely bowled her over.

transferReply: The second act bowled me over.

contrast: Bowl over is delighted astonishment; take aback is surprise that leaves you unsure.

第2幕には、心を打たれました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：bowl me over。ふつうは肯定的だが、物理的に倒す意味にもなる。
contrastJapanese: bowl over は感激を伴う驚き。take aback は戸惑いを伴う驚き。

meaning: Trap someone so they cannot move or choose freely.
easyEnglish: Trap someone so they cannot move or choose freely.
japanese: 身動きが取れないように、追い込む。
cue: A contract leaves no room to change suppliers. Describe the problem.
reply: The three-year term boxes us in completely.
transferCue: Describe a car park situation.
transferReply: Someone boxed me in and I waited forty minutes.
nuance: Separable: box me in. Used both for parked cars and for limited choices.
contrast: Box in removes room to move; tie down commits you to an obligation.

exampleTranslations.The three-year term boxes us in complete: 3年契約では、完全に身動きが取れなくなります。
exampleTranslations.Someone boxed me in and I waited forty m: 車を囲まれてしまい、40分待ちました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：box me in。駐車の場面にも、選択肢が狭まる状況にも使う。
contrastJapanese: box in は動ける余地をなくす。tie down は義務で縛る。

meaning: Leave a main route and go in another direction.
easyEnglish: Leave a main route and go in another direction.
japanese: 本筋から分かれて、別の方向へ進む。

reply: Follow the river until the path branches off to the left.

transferReply: We branched off into a long discussion about schools.
nuance: Intransitive. Used for roads and rivers, and for conversations that leave the main topic.
contrast: Branch off leaves the main line; branch out expands into something new.

exampleTranslations.Follow the river until the path branches: 道が左に分かれるところまで、川沿いに進んでください。
exampleTranslations.We branched off into a long discussion a: 話がそれて、学校の話で長くなりました。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。道や川のほか、本題からそれる会話にも使う。
contrastJapanese: branch off は本筋から分かれる。branch out は新しい分野へ広げる。

meaning: End a connection with a tradition, group or habit.
easyEnglish: End a connection with a tradition, group or habit.
japanese: これまでの慣習や関係を断ち切る。
cue: An organisation changed a long-standing practice. Describe it.
reply: The decision breaks with forty years of practice.

transferReply: We broke with tradition and had lunch outdoors.
nuance: Inseparable. Usually with tradition, convention, the past or a group.
contrast: Break with ends a connection; break off stops something already under way.

exampleTranslations.The decision breaks with forty years of: あの決定は、40年続いた慣行を断ち切るものです。
exampleTranslations.We broke with tradition and had lunch ou: 慣例を破って、昼食は外で取りました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。tradition、convention、the past、集団などと組み合わせるのがふつう。
contrastJapanese: break with は関係を断つ。break off は進行中のものを中断する。

meaning: Be completely full of a feeling or quality.
easyEnglish: Be completely full of a feeling or quality.
japanese: ある感情や性質に、満ちあふれている。
cue: A colleague returned from leave full of energy. Describe them.
reply: She came back brimming with ideas.
transferCue: Describe a child before a trip.
transferReply: He was brimming with excitement all morning.
nuance: Inseparable, usually in the -ing form. Used with feelings and qualities, not with objects.
contrast: Brim with is about feelings; be full of also works for physical contents.

彼女はアイデアにあふれて戻ってきました。
exampleTranslations.He was brimming with excitement all morn: 彼は午前中ずっと、わくわくした気持ちでいっぱいでした。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、ふつうは -ing 形で使う。物ではなく、感情や性質と組み合わせる。
contrastJapanese: brim with は感情について使う。be full of は中身が物でも使える。

meaning: Persuade someone to change their opinion.
easyEnglish: Persuade someone to change their opinion.
japanese: 説得して、考えを変えさせる。
cue: A colleague was against a plan and now supports it. Explain how.
reply: The cost comparison brought him round.
transferCue: Describe convincing a family member.
transferReply: It took a year to bring my father round to the idea.
nuance: Separable: bring him round. To introduces the opinion. American English says bring around.
contrast: Bring round changes an opinion; win over changes how someone feels about you.

費用の比較が、彼の考えを変えました。
exampleTranslations.It took a year to bring my father round: 父にその考えを受け入れてもらうまで、1年かかりました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：bring him round。意見は to で示す。アメリカ英語では bring around と言う。
contrastJapanese: bring round は意見を変えさせる。win over は自分への気持ちを変えさせる。

meaning: Fasten your seat belt.
easyEnglish: Fasten your seat belt.
japanese: シートベルトを締める。
cue: You are about to drive off with a passenger.
reply: Buckle up — it's a bumpy road for the first mile.
transferCue: Remind children in the back of a car.
transferReply: Everyone buckle up before we move.
nuance: Intransitive and mostly American; British English says belt up or put your seat belt on.
contrast: Buckle up fastens a belt; buckle down starts working seriously.

exampleTranslations.Buckle up — it's a bumpy road for the fi: シートベルトを締めてください。最初の1マイルは道が悪いです。
動き出す前に、全員シートベルトを締めてください。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で主にアメリカ英語。イギリス英語では belt up や put your seat belt on と言う。
contrastJapanese: buckle up はベルトを締める。buckle down は本腰を入れて取り組む。

meaning: Purchase someone's share so you own it completely.
easyEnglish: Purchase someone's share so you own it completely.
japanese: 持ち分を買い取って、自分のものにする。
cue: Two founders separated and one kept the business. Explain.
reply: She bought out her partner last spring.
transferCue: Describe how a larger company took over a small one.
transferReply: The group bought them out within a year.
nuance: Separable: buy them out. The noun is a buyout, written as one word.
contrast: Buy out acquires a share in a business; buy up purchases all the available stock.

彼女は昨春、共同経営者の持ち分を買い取りました。
そのグループは1年以内に、彼らを買収しました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：buy them out。名詞は buyout と1語で書く。
contrastJapanese: buy out は事業の持ち分を買い取る。buy up は出回っているものを買い占める。

meaning: Buy all or most of something that is available.
easyEnglish: Buy all or most of something that is available.
japanese: 出回っているものを、まとめて買い占める。
cue: A competitor purchased the entire supply. Report it.
reply: Someone bought up all the remaining stock overnight.
transferCue: Describe a property trend in an area.
transferReply: Investors have bought up most of the flats on that road.
nuance: Separable: buy it up. The up signals completeness — all of it, not just some.
contrast: Buy up takes everything available; stock up gathers a personal supply.

exampleTranslations.Someone bought up all the remaining stoc: 何者かが一晩で、残りの在庫をすべて買い占めました。
exampleTranslations.Investors have bought up most of the fla: 投資家が、あの通りの部屋の大半を買い占めています。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：buy it up。up は「全部」という完了のニュアンスを加える。
contrastJapanese: buy up は出回っている分を全部買う。stock up は自分用に買いだめする。

meaning: Think something is important to you.
easyEnglish: Think something is important to you.
japanese: 大切に思う。気にかける。
cue: Explain why you keep volunteering at a local centre.
reply: I care about what happens to that building.
transferCue: Tell a colleague why their view matters to you.
transferReply: I care about getting this right more than getting it done fast.
nuance: Inseparable. Care about is importance; care for is looking after someone or liking something.
contrast: Care about means something matters to you; care for means look after or like.

exampleTranslations.I care about what happens to that buildi: あの建物がどうなるかを、大切に思っています。
exampleTranslations.I care about getting this right more tha: 速く終えることより、きちんと仕上げることを大切に思っています。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。care about は重要視すること、care for は世話をする・好むこと。
contrastJapanese: care about は大切に思うこと。care for は世話をする、または好むこと。

meaning: Provide what a particular group needs.
easyEnglish: Provide what a particular group needs.
japanese: 特定の層の求めに応じて用意する。
cue: A guest asks whether an event suits families.
reply: The programme caters for children as well as adults.
transferCue: Describe a restaurant's menu.
transferReply: They cater for most dietary requirements.
nuance: Inseparable. British English prefers for, American to. Cater to can suggest indulging.
contrast: Cater for meets a need; cater to can suggest giving in to a demand.

exampleTranslations.The programme caters for children as wel: 催しは大人だけでなく、子ども向けにも用意されています。
exampleTranslations.They cater for most dietary requirements: あの店は、たいていの食事制限に対応しています。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。イギリス英語では for、アメリカ英語では to を好む。cater to は迎合の含みが出ることもある。
contrastJapanese: cater for は必要に応える。cater to は要求に迎合する含みを持つことがある。

meaning: Achieve or record something, such as a win or a total.
easyEnglish: Achieve or record something, such as a win or a total.
japanese: 勝利や記録を、積み上げる。
cue: A team has had a run of successes. Summarise.
reply: They've chalked up six wins in a row.
transferCue: Describe a milestone for a small shop.
transferReply: The café chalked up its thousandth customer this week.
nuance: Separable: chalk it up. Chalk something up to experience means treating a loss as a lesson.
contrast: Chalk up records an achievement; rack up often stresses a growing total.

彼らは6連勝を積み上げました。
exampleTranslations.The café chalked up its thousandth custo: 今週、あのカフェは1000人目のお客さんを迎えました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：chalk it up。chalk something up to experience なら、失敗を教訓として受け止める意味になる。
contrastJapanese: chalk up は成果を記録する。rack up は増えていく合計を強調することが多い。

meaning: Contact someone to get something you are waiting for.
easyEnglish: Contact someone to get something you are waiting for.
japanese: 催促して、返事や物を引き出す。
cue: An invoice has not been paid for six weeks. Say what you will do.
reply: I'll chase up the invoice this afternoon.
transferCue: Ask a colleague to follow a pending request.
transferReply: Could you chase them up about the signature?
nuance: Separable: chase them up. British; American English usually says follow up.
contrast: Chase up presses for something overdue; follow up continues an earlier contact.

exampleTranslations.I'll chase up the invoice this afternoon: 午後に、その請求について催促します。
exampleTranslations.Could you chase them up about the signat: 署名の件、先方に催促してもらえますか。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：chase them up。イギリス英語で、アメリカ英語ではふつう follow up と言う。
contrastJapanese: chase up は遅れているものを催促する。follow up は前のやり取りの続きをする。

meaning: Think carefully about something for a while.
easyEnglish: Think carefully about something for a while.
japanese: しばらくじっくり考える。
cue: A colleague wants an answer now but you need time.
reply: Let me chew it over tonight and answer tomorrow.
transferCue: Describe how you handled a difficult choice.
transferReply: I chewed over both options for a fortnight.
nuance: Separable: chew it over. Informal, and it suggests unhurried private thinking.
contrast: Chew over is unhurried reflection; think through follows consequences to the end.

exampleTranslations.Let me chew it over tonight and answer t: 今夜じっくり考えて、明日お返事します。
exampleTranslations.I chewed over both options for a fortnig: 2週間、両方の選択肢をじっくり考えました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：chew it over。くだけた表現で、急がずひとりで考える含みがある。
contrastJapanese: chew over はじっくり考えること。think through は結果まで筋道を追うこと。

meaning: Gradually reduce or weaken something.
easyEnglish: Gradually reduce or weaken something.
japanese: 少しずつ削り取るように、弱めていく。
cue: Repeated small cuts have reduced a service. Describe the pattern.
reply: Each year's cut chips away at what the team can do.
transferCue: Describe steady progress on a large task.
transferReply: I chip away at the backlog for an hour each morning.
nuance: Inseparable. It can describe damage or patient progress, depending on what is reduced.
contrast: Chip away at is gradual reduction; wear down exhausts resistance over time.

exampleTranslations.Each year's cut chips away at what the t: 毎年の削減が、チームにできることを少しずつ削っています。
exampleTranslations.I chip away at the backlog for an hour e: 毎朝1時間ずつ、たまった作業を少しずつ片づけています。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。削られる対象によって、損なう意味にも、着実に進める意味にもなる。
contrastJapanese: chip away at は少しずつ削ること。wear down は時間をかけて抵抗を消耗させること。

meaning: Force yourself not to show a strong emotion.
easyEnglish: Force yourself not to show a strong emotion.
japanese: こみ上げる感情を、必死にこらえる。
cue: Describe someone speaking at a farewell.
reply: He choked back tears and finished the speech.
transferCue: Describe your own reaction to unfair criticism.
transferReply: I choked back a reply I would have regretted.
nuance: Separable: choke it back. Usually with tears, anger or a reply.
contrast: Choke back holds an emotion in; hold back can also mean withholding information.

exampleTranslations.He choked back tears and finished the sp: 彼は涙をこらえて、挨拶を最後まで続けました。
exampleTranslations.I choked back a reply I would have regre: 後悔しそうな返事を、ぐっとこらえました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：choke it back。tears、anger、a reply などと組み合わせるのがふつう。
contrastJapanese: choke back は感情を抑える。hold back は情報を出さない意味にもなる。

meaning: Produce large amounts quickly, often without much care.
easyEnglish: Produce large amounts quickly, often without much care.
japanese: 次々と大量に作り出す。
cue: A studio releases similar products constantly. Describe it.
reply: They churn out three of these a month.
transferCue: Describe your own writing during a deadline week.
transferReply: I churned out four drafts and kept one.
nuance: Separable: churn them out. Usually implies quantity at the cost of quality.
contrast: Churn out stresses quick quantity; turn out is neutral about how something was produced.

あそこは、この種のものを月に3つ量産しています。
草稿を4本量産して、1本だけ残しました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：churn them out。質を犠牲にした量産という含みがあることが多い。
contrastJapanese: churn out は速さと量を強調する。turn out は作り方について中立。

meaning: Admit you were wrong and change your position.
easyEnglish: Admit you were wrong and change your position.
japanese: 前言を撤回して、立場を引っ込める。
cue: A firm public position was reversed. Describe it.
reply: The board climbed down after the members objected.
transferCue: Describe your own change of position in a dispute.
transferReply: I had to climb down once I'd seen the contract.
nuance: Intransitive. The noun is a climbdown. It implies a visible, public reversal.
contrast: Climb down reverses a public position; back down stops pressing a demand.

exampleTranslations.The board climbed down after the members: 会員の反対を受けて、理事会は主張を撤回しました。
exampleTranslations.I had to climb down once I'd seen the co: 契約書を見て、主張を引っ込めるしかありませんでした。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。名詞は climbdown。人前での、目に見える撤回という含みがある。
contrastJapanese: climb down は公の主張を撤回する。back down は要求を引っ込める。

meaning: Separate an area so it cannot be entered.
easyEnglish: Separate an area so it cannot be entered.
japanese: 区域を仕切って、入れないようにする。
cue: Part of a building is unsafe. Explain the arrangement.
reply: We'll close off the east wing until the survey is done.
transferCue: Describe a park during an event.
transferReply: They closed off the lawn for the concert.
nuance: Separable: close it off. It also describes closing off an option or a possibility.
contrast: Close off seals an area; close down ends an operation entirely.

exampleTranslations.We'll close off the east wing until the: 調査が終わるまで、東棟は閉鎖します。
exampleTranslations.They closed off the lawn for the concert: コンサートのために、芝生は立ち入り禁止になりました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：close it off。選択肢や可能性を閉ざす意味にも使う。
contrastJapanese: close off は区域を封鎖する。close down は事業そのものを終わらせる。

meaning: Share the cost of something among several people.
easyEnglish: Share the cost of something among several people.
japanese: 何人かでお金を出し合う。
cue: A team wants to buy a leaving gift. Suggest the method.
reply: Shall we club together for something better?
transferCue: Describe how neighbours funded a repair.
transferReply: Six households clubbed together to fix the fence.
nuance: Intransitive and British. For or to introduces the purpose, and it implies three or more people.
contrast: Club together pools money from a group; go halves splits a cost between two.

exampleTranslations.Shall we club together for something bet: みんなで出し合って、もう少しいいものにしませんか。
exampleTranslations.Six households clubbed together to fix t: 6世帯でお金を出し合って、塀を直しました。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、イギリス英語。目的は for か to で示し、3人以上を想定する。
contrastJapanese: club together は複数人で出し合う。go halves は2人で半分ずつにする。

meaning: Search something very carefully.
easyEnglish: Search something very carefully.
japanese: すみずみまで丹念に調べる。
cue: You need to find one figure in a long report. Describe the task.
reply: I combed through the appendix and found it on page sixty.
transferCue: Describe looking for a lost item.
transferReply: We combed through every drawer in the house.
nuance: Inseparable. It emphasises thoroughness rather than speed.
contrast: Comb through is exhaustive searching; flick through is quick, casual looking.

exampleTranslations.I combed through the appendix and found: 付録をすみずみまで調べて、60ページで見つけました。
exampleTranslations.We combed through every drawer in the ho: 家じゅうの引き出しを、一つ残らず調べました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。速さではなく、徹底ぶりを強調する。
contrastJapanese: comb through は徹底的に調べる。flick through はざっと目を通す。

meaning: Damage the relationship between two people.
easyEnglish: Damage the relationship between two people.
japanese: 二人のあいだに入って、関係を損なう。
cue: A disagreement about money is affecting two friends. Warn gently.
reply: Don't let one invoice come between you.
transferCue: Describe a family that stayed close despite a dispute.
transferReply: Nothing has ever come between those two sisters.
nuance: Inseparable, and it needs two people or a plural. The cause is the subject.
contrast: Come between divides two people; get in the way of blocks an activity.

請求書ひとつで、二人の関係を壊さないでください。
exampleTranslations.Nothing has ever come between those two: あの姉妹のあいだを裂いたものは、今まで何もありません。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、二人または複数が必要。主語は原因のほう。
contrastJapanese: come between は二人の仲を裂く。get in the way of は物事の妨げになる。

meaning: Criticise or punish someone severely.
easyEnglish: Criticise or punish someone severely.
japanese: 厳しく叱責する。厳しく処分する。
cue: A manager reacted harshly to a small mistake. Describe it.
reply: They came down on him hard for a typo.
transferCue: Describe how an authority treats a rule.
transferReply: The council comes down on anyone who parks there.
frame: Come down on someone for something
nuance: Inseparable, often with hard. For introduces the reason.
contrast: Come down on is harsh criticism; pull up is a milder correction.

誤字ひとつで、彼は厳しく叱責されました。
exampleTranslations.The council comes down on anyone who par: 自治体は、そこに駐車した人を厳しく取り締まります。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、hard を伴うことが多い。理由は for で示す。
contrastJapanese: come down on は厳しい叱責。pull up はもっと軽い注意。

meaning: Say something unexpected or surprising.
easyEnglish: Say something unexpected or surprising.
japanese: 思いがけないことを、ふいに口にする。
cue: A quiet colleague made a very funny remark. Describe it.
reply: He came out with the best line of the evening.
transferCue: Describe a child's surprising question.
transferReply: She came out with a question nobody could answer.
nuance: Inseparable. It suggests surprise at what was said, not deliberate announcement.
contrast: Come out with is a surprising remark; come up with is inventing an idea.

exampleTranslations.He came out with the best line of the ev: 彼が、その晩いちばん面白い一言を放ちました。
exampleTranslations.She came out with a question nobody coul: 彼女は、誰も答えられない質問をふいに口にしました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。計画的な発表ではなく、発言の意外さを表す。
contrastJapanese: come out with は意外な発言。come up with は考えを思いつくこと。

meaning: Try to be more successful than someone else.
easyEnglish: Try to be more successful than someone else.
japanese: 相手より上を目指して競う。
cue: A small firm faces much larger rivals. Describe its position.
reply: We can't compete with them on price, so we compete on service.
transferCue: Describe two shops on the same street.
transferReply: The two bakeries compete with each other quite happily.
nuance: Inseparable. On introduces the basis of competition; for introduces the prize.
contrast: Compete with names the rival; compete for names what is being contested.

exampleTranslations.We can't compete with them on price, so: 価格では勝負できないので、サービスで競っています。
exampleTranslations.The two bakeries compete with each other: あの2軒のパン屋は、和やかに競い合っています。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。競う基準は on、争う対象は for で示す。
contrastJapanese: compete with は競争相手を示す。compete for は争う対象を示す。

meaning: Have to deal with a difficulty.
easyEnglish: Have to deal with a difficulty.
japanese: やっかいな問題に、対処しなければならない。
cue: A project has several obstacles at once. Summarise them.
reply: We're contending with a strike and a supply delay.
transferCue: Describe a commute in winter.
transferReply: Most mornings I contend with ice and a late bus.
nuance: Inseparable and slightly formal. The object is always a difficulty, never a benefit.
contrast: Contend with is forced to handle a problem; cope with focuses on managing the strain.

exampleTranslations.We're contending with a strike and a sup: ストライキと供給の遅れの両方に対処しています。
exampleTranslations.Most mornings I contend with ice and a l: たいていの朝は、凍結とバスの遅れに対処しています。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない、やや改まった表現。目的語はつねに困りごとで、よいことには使わない。
contrastJapanese: contend with は問題への対処を迫られること。cope with は負担をこなすことに焦点がある。

meaning: Arrange for outside people to do work for you.
easyEnglish: Arrange for outside people to do work for you.
japanese: 仕事を外部に委託する。
cue: A task no longer suits your team. Propose a change.
reply: We could contract out the translation and keep editing in-house.
transferCue: Describe how a council handles refuse collection.
transferReply: The service was contracted out three years ago.
nuance: Separable: contract it out. To introduces the supplier. Outsource is the one-word equivalent.
contrast: Contract out sends work outside; farm out often suggests distributing it informally.

exampleTranslations.We could contract out the translation an: 翻訳は外部に委託して、編集は社内に残すことができます。
exampleTranslations.The service was contracted out three yea: その業務は、3年前に外部委託されました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：contract it out。委託先は to で示す。1語の同義語は outsource。
contrastJapanese: contract out は正式に外部委託する。farm out は非公式に割り振る含みを持つことが多い。

meaning: Put a barrier around an area to keep people out.
easyEnglish: Put a barrier around an area to keep people out.
japanese: 規制線を張って、周囲を立ち入り禁止にする。
cue: Describe what you saw on the way to work.
reply: Police had cordoned off the square.
transferCue: Describe a filming location in a city.
transferReply: They cordoned off two streets for the shoot.
nuance: Separable: cordon it off. Usually used about police, emergency services or organisers.
contrast: Cordon off uses a visible barrier; block off simply prevents access.

警察が広場に規制線を張っていました。
exampleTranslations.They cordoned off two streets for the sh: 撮影のために、通りを2本封鎖していました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：cordon it off。警察や消防、主催者について使うのがふつう。
contrastJapanese: cordon off は目に見える規制線を張る。block off は単に通れなくする。

meaning: Finally understand something.
easyEnglish: Finally understand something.
japanese: ようやく気づく。合点がいく。
cue: You understood a joke after everyone else. Admit it.
reply: It took me a minute to cotton on.
transferCue: Describe how customers noticed a price change.
transferReply: People cottoned on to the new charge quite quickly.
nuance: Intransitive and informal, mostly British. To introduces what you realise.
contrast: Cotton on is delayed realisation; catch on can also mean becoming popular.

気づくまで、ちょっと時間がかかりました。
exampleTranslations.People cottoned on to the new charge qui: 新しい料金には、みんなすぐ気づきました。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞のくだけた表現で、主にイギリス英語。気づいた内容は to で示す。
contrastJapanese: cotton on は遅れて気づくこと。catch on には「流行する」の意味もある。

meaning: Pay money reluctantly.
easyEnglish: Pay money reluctantly.
japanese: しぶしぶ支払う。
cue: An unexpected fee appeared on a booking. React.
reply: We had to cough up another thirty pounds for the bags.
transferCue: Describe settling a shared bill.
transferReply: Everyone coughed up eventually.
nuance: Separable: cough it up. Informal and always implies reluctance.
contrast: Cough up is reluctant payment; shell out stresses that the amount was large.

exampleTranslations.We had to cough up another thirty pounds: 荷物代として、さらに30ポンド払わされました。
結局、全員がしぶしぶ支払いました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：cough it up。くだけた表現で、つねに気が進まない含みがある。
contrastJapanese: cough up はしぶしぶ払う。shell out は金額の大きさを強調する。

meaning: Exclude someone or something from a plan.
easyEnglish: Exclude someone or something from a plan.
japanese: 計画から外す。数に入れない。
cue: A friend cannot join a weekend trip. Respond to their message.
reply: Count me out this time, I'm afraid.
transferCue: Rule out one option in a discussion.
transferReply: We can count out the June date — the hall is booked.
nuance: Separable: count me out. The opposite is count me in. It also means counting money aloud.
contrast: Count out excludes from a plan; rule out excludes a possibility.

今回は、私は外してください。
exampleTranslations.We can count out the June date — the hal: 6月の日程は外しましょう。会場が埋まっています。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：count me out。反対は count me in。お金を数え出す、という別の意味もある。
contrastJapanese: count out は計画から人を外す。rule out は可能性を排除する。

meaning: Continue working quickly.
easyEnglish: Continue working quickly.
japanese: 作業をどんどん進める。
cue: A break is over and there is a lot left. Encourage the team.
reply: Let's crack on — two hours should finish it.
transferCue: Reply to a message during a busy afternoon.
transferReply: I'd better crack on. I'll call you this evening.
nuance: Intransitive, informal and British. With introduces the task.
contrast: Crack on is getting on quickly; press on emphasises continuing despite difficulty.

exampleTranslations.Let's crack on — two hours should finish: どんどん進めましょう。2時間あれば終わります。
exampleTranslations.I'd better crack on. I'll call you this: 作業を進めます。夕方に電話します。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞のくだけたイギリス英語。作業の対象は with で示す。
contrastJapanese: crack on は手早く進めること。press on は困難でも続けることを強調する。

meaning: Fall asleep quickly because you are exhausted.
easyEnglish: Fall asleep quickly because you are exhausted.
japanese: 疲れ果てて、そのまま眠り込む。
cue: Describe the end of a long travel day.
reply: I crashed out at eight and slept until morning.
transferCue: Describe a friend after a night shift.
transferReply: He crashes out on the sofa most Saturdays.
nuance: Intransitive and informal. In sport it also means being knocked out of a competition.
contrast: Crash out is falling asleep from exhaustion; nod off is drifting off unintentionally.

exampleTranslations.I crashed out at eight and slept until m: 8時には眠り込んで、朝まで寝ていました。
exampleTranslations.He crashes out on the sofa most Saturday: 彼はたいてい土曜に、ソファで眠り込んでいます。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞のくだけた表現。スポーツでは「大会から敗退する」の意味にもなる。
contrastJapanese: crash out は疲れて眠り込むこと。nod off はうとうとしてしまうこと。

meaning: Gradually start to appear, usually unwanted.
easyEnglish: Gradually start to appear, usually unwanted.
japanese: いつの間にか、じわじわと入り込む。
cue: Small errors have appeared in a long document. Describe how.
reply: Mistakes creep in when we copy rows by hand.
transferCue: Describe a change of tone in a discussion.
transferReply: A bit of impatience crept in towards the end.
nuance: Intransitive. Creep is irregular: crept. The unwanted thing is the subject.
contrast: Creep in appears gradually and unnoticed; set in means a condition becomes established.

exampleTranslations.Mistakes creep in when we copy rows by h: 手作業で行をコピーすると、いつの間にか誤りが入り込みます。
exampleTranslations.A bit of impatience crept in towards the: 終わりのほうで、いらだちが少しにじみ始めました。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。creep は不規則変化で crept。主語は望まないもののほう。
contrastJapanese: creep in は気づかぬうちに現れる。set in はある状態が定着する。

meaning: Take so much space that other things have no room.
easyEnglish: Take so much space that other things have no room.
japanese: 場所を占めて、ほかのものを締め出す。
cue: One topic dominated a whole meeting. Describe the effect.
reply: The budget item crowded out everything else.
transferCue: Describe a high street changing.
transferReply: Chains have crowded out most of the independent shops.
nuance: Separable: crowd them out. The dominant thing is the subject.
contrast: Crowd out squeezes others out by volume; edge out wins narrowly over a rival.

exampleTranslations.The budget item crowded out everything e: 予算の議題が、ほかをすべて押しのけてしまいました。
exampleTranslations.Chains have crowded out most of the inde: チェーン店が、個人商店の大半を締め出しました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：crowd them out。主語は場所を占めているほう。
contrastJapanese: crowd out は量で押しのける。edge out はわずかの差で相手を抑える。

meaning: Cancel something you had agreed to do.
easyEnglish: Cancel something you had agreed to do.
japanese: 一度引き受けたことを、取りやめる。
cue: Someone withdrew from a commitment at the last minute. Describe it.
reply: Two of them cried off the day before.
transferCue: Explain why you had to withdraw from an event.
transferReply: I had to cry off because of a family thing.
nuance: Intransitive and British. It implies letting someone down, not simply declining an invitation.
contrast: Cry off cancels a commitment; turn down declines before agreeing.

2人が前日になって取りやめました。
exampleTranslations.I had to cry off because of a family thi: 家の事情で、取りやめるしかありませんでした。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、イギリス英語。単なる辞退ではなく、相手の当てを外す含みがある。
contrastJapanese: cry off は引き受けたあとで取りやめる。turn down は引き受ける前に断る。

meaning: Sit or lie with your arms and legs pulled close to you.
easyEnglish: Sit or lie with your arms and legs pulled close to you.
japanese: 体を丸めて、くつろぐ。
cue: Describe your ideal rainy afternoon.
reply: I like to curl up with a book and ignore the weather.
transferCue: Describe a cat in winter.
transferReply: She curls up next to the radiator all day.
nuance: Intransitive. With introduces what you settle down with, often a book or a drink.
contrast: Curl up is a cosy posture; settle down is about becoming calm or staying in one place.

exampleTranslations.I like to curl up with a book and ignore: 本を持って体を丸め、天気は気にせず過ごすのが好きです。
exampleTranslations.She curls up next to the radiator all da: あの子は一日中、暖房のそばで丸くなっています。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。一緒に過ごすものは with で示し、本や飲み物などが来ることが多い。

contrastJapanese: delight in は持続的な喜び。enjoy はもっと日常的な語。

meaning: Find information that was hidden or forgotten.

meaning: Turn and go back the way you came.

meaning: Make someone or something worse or less successful.
