exampleTranslations.She put the advice into practice immedia: 彼女はその助言を、すぐ実践に移しました。

nuanceJapanese: 目的語は put と into のあいだに置く。ここでの practice に冠詞は付かない。

meaning: Show how important something really is by comparison.
easyEnglish: Show how important something really is by comparison.
japanese: 比べることで、本当の重要度を分からせる。
cue: A small complaint follows news of something serious.
reply: That rather puts our problems into perspective.
transferCue: Compare two figures.
transferReply: One number puts the whole budget into perspective.
nuance: The object goes between put and into. Perspective takes no article.

exampleTranslations.That rather puts our problems into persp: それを聞くと、こちらの悩みは小さく思えます。
exampleTranslations.One number puts the whole budget into pe: その数字ひとつで、予算全体の大きさが分かります。

nuanceJapanese: 目的語は put と into のあいだに置く。perspective に冠詞は付かない。

meaning: Start writing something.
easyEnglish: Start writing something.
japanese: 実際に、書き始める。
cue: Someone has been planning to write for months.
reply: He finally put pen to paper in January.
transferCue: Describe starting a difficult letter.
transferReply: It took me a week to put pen to paper.
nuance: No articles inside the phrase. Used even when the writing is done on a screen.

彼は1月に、ようやく書き始めました。
書き始めるまでに、1週間かかりました。

nuanceJapanese: 句の中に冠詞は入らない。画面で書く場合にも使う。

meaning: Be so much better that the other thing looks poor.
easyEnglish: Be so much better that the other thing looks poor.
japanese: 引き比べて、見劣りさせてしまう。
cue: An amateur effort was better than a professional one.
reply: Her cake puts the bakery to shame.
transferCue: Describe a surprising performance.
transferReply: The junior team put the seniors to shame.
nuance: The object goes between put and to. Shame takes no article. It compliments by comparison.

彼女のケーキは、あのパン屋が見劣りするほどです。
exampleTranslations.The junior team put the seniors to shame: 下級生のチームが、上級生を圧倒しました。

nuanceJapanese: 目的語は put と to のあいだに置く。shame に冠詞は付かない。比較によってほめる表現。

meaning: Resist strongly instead of giving in.
easyEnglish: Resist strongly instead of giving in.
japanese: 簡単には引き下がらず、抵抗する。
cue: A team lost but made it difficult.
reply: They lost, but they put up a fight.
transferCue: Describe resisting a decision.
transferReply: The residents put up a fight over the closure.
nuance: Fight takes a. Usually admiring of the resistance, even when it fails.

負けはしましたが、彼らはよく抵抗しました。
exampleTranslations.The residents put up a fight over the cl: 住民は閉鎖に対して、強く抵抗しました。

nuanceJapanese: fight には a を付ける。失敗した場合でも、抵抗を肯定的に評価することが多い。

meaning: Do something with full commitment and feeling.
easyEnglish: Do something with full commitment and feeling.
japanese: 心を込めて、全力で取り組む。
cue: Someone worked on something with real care.
reply: She put her heart into that garden.
transferCue: Encourage genuine effort.
transferReply: Put your heart into it and it'll show.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. It describes emotional commitment, not just hard work.

彼女はあの庭に、心を込めていました。
心を込めれば、それは伝わります。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。単なる労力ではなく、気持ちの込め方を表す。

meaning: Start performing at a higher level.
easyEnglish: Start performing at a higher level.
japanese: 一段上の水準に、自分を引き上げる。
cue: Standards have risen and the team must respond.
reply: We'll have to raise our game next season.
transferCue: Praise an improvement.
transferReply: He raised his game after the first review.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Up your game means the same and is more informal.

exampleTranslations.We'll have to raise our game next season: 来季は、もう一段上を目指す必要があります。
exampleTranslations.He raised his game after the first revie: 最初の評価のあと、彼は一段上の働きを見せました。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。up your game も同じ意味で、よりくだけた言い方。

meaning: Come together to support someone in difficulty.
easyEnglish: Come together to support someone in difficulty.
japanese: 困っている人のために、みんなで力を合わせる。
cue: A neighbour had an accident and got help.
reply: The whole street rallied round after the fire.
transferCue: Describe support at work.
transferReply: The team rallied round while she was away.
nuance: British uses round, American around. It describes a group, not one helper.
contrast: Rally round is a group gathering to help; stand by is staying loyal alone.

exampleTranslations.The whole street rallied round after the: 火事のあと、通りじゅうが力を合わせました。
exampleTranslations.The team rallied round while she was awa: 彼女の不在中、チームが結束して支えました。

nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語は round、アメリカ英語は around。一人ではなく、集団の支援を表す。
contrastJapanese: rally round は皆で助けに集まる。stand by は一人でも味方であり続ける。

meaning: Study a subject by reading about it.
easyEnglish: Study a subject by reading about it.
japanese: 本や資料を読んで、下調べする。
cue: You need background before a meeting.
reply: I'll read up on the regulations tonight.
transferCue: Prepare for a trip.
transferReply: She read up on the area before going.
nuance: Inseparable; on introduces the subject. It implies deliberate preparation.
contrast: Read up on prepares by reading; brush up on refreshes what you knew.

今夜、規制について調べておきます。
彼女は行く前に、その地域について調べました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、対象は on で示す。意識的な準備であることを含意する。
contrastJapanese: read up on は読んで備える。brush up on は忘れかけた知識を戻す。

meaning: Experience the results of your own earlier actions.
easyEnglish: Experience the results of your own earlier actions.
japanese: 自分のまいた種を、自分で刈り取る。
cue: Earlier carelessness has caused a problem.
reply: We're reaping what we sowed last summer.
transferCue: Describe a positive result of effort.
transferReply: She's reaping what she sowed over ten years.
nuance: Sow is irregular: sowed, sown. Usually about bad consequences, though it works for good ones.

去年の夏にまいた種を、今刈り取っています。
exampleTranslations.She's reaping what she sowed over ten ye: 彼女は10年かけてまいた種を、今刈り取っています。

nuanceJapanese: sow は不規則変化で sowed、sown。ふつうは悪い結果だが、よい結果にも使える。

meaning: Bring something under control.
easyEnglish: Bring something under control.
japanese: 手綱を引いて、抑え込む。
cue: Spending has grown beyond plan.
reply: We need to rein in the travel budget.
transferCue: Describe controlling enthusiasm.
transferReply: He reined in his ambitions for a year.
nuance: Separable: rein it in. Spelled rein, from horse riding, not reign.
contrast: Rein in slows something that is running away; hold back keeps it from starting.

出張費を、抑え込む必要があります。
彼は1年、野心を抑えました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：rein it in。つづりは reign ではなく rein で、乗馬に由来する。
contrastJapanese: rein in は暴走しかけたものを抑える。hold back は始めさせない。

meaning: Refuse to be affected by something petty.
easyEnglish: Refuse to be affected by something petty.
japanese: くだらないことに、乗らずにいる。
cue: Someone is being provoked online.
reply: It's better to rise above it and say nothing.
transferCue: Praise someone's restraint.
transferReply: She rose above the criticism entirely.
nuance: Rise is irregular: rose, risen. It praises restraint, not indifference.

exampleTranslations.It's better to rise above it and say not: 相手にせず、何も言わないほうがいいです。
彼女はその批判に、まったく動じませんでした。

nuanceJapanese: rise は不規則変化で rose、risen。無関心ではなく、自制をほめる表現。

meaning: Completely reliable or firm.
easyEnglish: Completely reliable or firm.
japanese: びくともしないほど、確かである。
cue: Evidence for a claim is very strong.
reply: The data behind this is rock solid.
transferCue: Describe a dependable colleague.
transferReply: He's been rock solid all through the project.
nuance: Hyphenated before a noun. Used for evidence, structures and people alike.

これを支えるデータは、非常に確かです。
exampleTranslations.He's been rock solid all through the pro: 彼はこの企画の間ずっと、頼りになりました。

nuanceJapanese: 名詞の前ではハイフンでつなぐ。証拠にも構造物にも人にも使う。

meaning: Get ready to do hard work.
easyEnglish: Get ready to do hard work.
japanese: 腕まくりして、本気で取りかかる。
cue: A big clear-out is about to start.
reply: Let's roll up our sleeves and start with the shed.
transferCue: Describe a leader joining in.
transferReply: She rolled up her sleeves and helped carry boxes.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject and sleeves is plural. It signals willingness, not just effort.

exampleTranslations.Let's roll up our sleeves and start with: 腕まくりして、まず物置から始めましょう。
exampleTranslations.She rolled up her sleeves and helped car: 彼女は腕まくりして、箱運びを手伝いました。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせ、sleeves は複数形。労力だけでなく、進んで取り組む姿勢を示す。

meaning: Simple and not refined, but good enough.
easyEnglish: Simple and not refined, but good enough.
japanese: 作りは粗いが、用は足りる。
cue: A quick prototype is being shown.
reply: It's rough and ready, but it shows the idea.
transferCue: Describe a simple meal.
transferReply: Supper was rough and ready and very good.
nuance: Fixed word order. It excuses the roughness by pointing at usefulness.

exampleTranslations.It's rough and ready, but it shows the i: 粗い作りですが、考えは伝わります。
exampleTranslations.Supper was rough and ready and very good: 夕食は簡素でしたが、とてもおいしかったです。

nuanceJapanese: 語順は固定。粗さを、実用性で埋め合わせる言い方。

meaning: Keep reminding someone of something embarrassing.
easyEnglish: Keep reminding someone of something embarrassing.
japanese: 失敗を、何度も蒸し返して追い打ちをかける。
cue: A friend keeps mentioning your mistake.
reply: All right, you don't have to rub it in.
transferCue: Describe teasing after a loss.
transferReply: They won and then rubbed it in all evening.
nuance: Fixed with it. Informal, and usually said in protest by the person being teased.

分かりましたから、何度も言わないでください。
exampleTranslations.They won and then rubbed it in all eveni: 彼らは勝ったうえに、一晩中それを言い続けました。

nuanceJapanese: it を伴う固定表現。くだけた言い方で、からかわれる側が抗議として使うことが多い。

meaning: Control a group very strictly.
easyEnglish: Control a group very strictly.
japanese: 鉄の規律で、厳しく支配する。
cue: Describe a very strict former manager.
reply: He ruled with an iron fist for a decade.
transferCue: Contrast a gentler style.
transferReply: She doesn't rule with an iron fist, and it works.
nuance: British also says with a rod of iron. Always critical of the severity.
aliases: rule with a rod of iron

彼は10年間、鉄の規律で組織を治めました。
exampleTranslations.She doesn't rule with an iron fist, and: 彼女は力で押さえつけませんが、それでうまくいっています。

nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語では with a rod of iron とも言う。その厳しさへの批判をつねに含む。

meaning: Avoid something because it frightens you.
easyEnglish: Avoid something because it frightens you.
japanese: 怖くて、逃げ出したくなる。
cue: Someone dislikes public speaking intensely.
reply: He'd run a mile rather than give a speech.
transferCue: Describe avoiding commitment.
transferReply: Mention a two-year contract and she'd run a mile.
nuance: Usually with would. It exaggerates the reluctance rather than describing real running.

exampleTranslations.He'd run a mile rather than give a speec: 彼は挨拶をするくらいなら、逃げ出すでしょう。
exampleTranslations.Mention a two-year contract and she'd ru: 2年契約と言えば、彼女は逃げ出すでしょう。

nuanceJapanese: ふつう would と使う。実際に走るのではなく、嫌がり方を誇張する表現。

meaning: Be felt very strongly, below the surface.
easyEnglish: Be felt very strongly, below the surface.
japanese: 表には出ないが、根が深い。
cue: An old disagreement still affects a group.
reply: The resentment runs deep in that team.
transferCue: Describe a family tradition.
transferReply: Loyalty runs deep in that family.
nuance: The feeling is the subject. Deep is an adverb here, not deeply.

あのチームでは、わだかまりが根深く残っています。
あの家族には、深い結束があります。

nuanceJapanese: 主語は感情のほう。ここでの deep は副詞で、deeply とは言わない。

meaning: Have almost none of something left.
easyEnglish: Have almost none of something left.
japanese: 残りが少なくなる。
cue: Supplies are nearly gone before the end of a week.
reply: We're running short of paper again.
transferCue: Describe limited time.
transferReply: We ran short of time at the end.
nuance: Of introduces what is nearly gone. Run out of means it has finished completely.

また紙が足りなくなってきました。
最後は、時間が足りなくなりました。

nuanceJapanese: 不足しているものは of で示す。完全になくなった場合は run out of を使う。

meaning: Only just succeed in passing something.
easyEnglish: Only just succeed in passing something.
japanese: ぎりぎりで、なんとか通る。
cue: An exam result was barely a pass.
reply: I scraped through the second paper.
transferCue: Describe a narrow qualification.
transferReply: They scraped through to the final round.
nuance: Intransitive or with an object. It reports a narrow pass, which can sound modest or relieved.
contrast: Scrape through passes by the narrowest margin; sail through passes easily.

2科目めは、ぎりぎりで通りました。
彼らはぎりぎりで、決勝に進みました。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞でも目的語付きでも使う。かろうじての合格を表し、謙遜や安堵の響きになる。
contrastJapanese: scrape through はぎりぎりで通る。sail through は楽々と通る。

meaning: Be published, released or brought into use.
easyEnglish: Be published, released or brought into use.
japanese: 世に出る。日の目を見る。
cue: A project was finished but never released.
reply: That design never saw the light of day.
transferCue: Describe a long-delayed book.
transferReply: The manuscript finally saw the light of day in 2024.
nuance: See is irregular: saw, seen. Often in the negative about work that was shelved.

あの設計は、ついに日の目を見ませんでした。
exampleTranslations.The manuscript finally saw the light of: その原稿は2024年に、ようやく世に出ました。

nuanceJapanese: see は不規則変化で saw、seen。棚上げされた仕事について、否定形で使うことが多い。

meaning: Be useful for something.
easyEnglish: Be useful for something.
japanese: 何らかの役に立っている。
cue: An odd-looking rule turns out to be useful.
reply: The extra check does serve a purpose.
transferCue: Question something useless.
transferReply: I'm not sure this form serves any purpose.
nuance: Purpose takes a, or any in the negative. It defends or questions usefulness.

あの追加確認にも、ちゃんと意味があります。
exampleTranslations.I'm not sure this form serves any purpos: この書式に、意味があるとは思えません。

nuanceJapanese: purpose には a を付け、否定形では any を使う。有用性を擁護、または疑う表現。

meaning: Do something that others may later point to as an example.
easyEnglish: Do something that others may later point to as an example.
japanese: 前例を作る。
cue: An exception could be used to justify future requests.
reply: Approving this sets a precedent we'd regret.
transferCue: Describe a landmark decision.
transferReply: The ruling set a precedent for similar cases.
nuance: Set is irregular and unchanged: set. For introduces what follows, and it often warns.

exampleTranslations.Approving this sets a precedent we'd reg: これを認めれば、後悔する前例を作ることになります。
exampleTranslations.The ruling set a precedent for similar c: あの判決は、同種の事案の前例となりました。

nuanceJapanese: set は不規則変化で形が変わらない。続くものは for で示し、警告として使うことが多い。

meaning: See someone or something for the first time.
easyEnglish: See someone or something for the first time.
japanese: 初めて目にする。
cue: Describe a first impression from years ago.
reply: I knew from the moment I set eyes on it.
transferCue: Describe never having seen something.
transferReply: I'd never set eyes on the place before.
nuance: Eyes is always plural. Usually with first, never or the moment, and set never changes.

ひと目見た瞬間から、分かっていました。
その場所を目にするのは、初めてでした。

nuanceJapanese: eyes はつねに複数形。first、never、the moment と使うことが多く、set は形が変わらない。

meaning: Start a process that then continues.
easyEnglish: Start a process that then continues.
japanese: 動き出す仕組みを、始動させる。
cue: A decision triggered a series of steps.
reply: That signature set the whole process in motion.
transferCue: Describe starting a long procedure.
transferReply: We set the application in motion in March.
nuance: The object goes between set and in. Motion takes no article.

exampleTranslations.That signature set the whole process in: あの署名が、一連の手続きを動かし始めました。
exampleTranslations.We set the application in motion in Marc: 3月に、申請の手続きを動かし始めました。

nuanceJapanese: 目的語は set と in のあいだに置く。motion に冠詞は付かない。

meaning: Support something that is becoming weak.
easyEnglish: Support something that is becoming weak.
japanese: 弱ってきたものを、下支えする。
cue: A struggling part of a business needs help.
reply: The loan shores up the business until spring.
transferCue: Describe strengthening an argument.
transferReply: Two more examples would shore up the case.
nuance: Separable: shore it up. From building work, and it implies the thing was weakening.
contrast: Shore up supports something weakening; build up makes something stronger over time.

exampleTranslations.The loan shores up the business until sp: その融資が、春まで事業を下支えします。
exampleTranslations.Two more examples would shore up the cas: 例をあと2つ足せば、論拠が固まります。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：shore it up。建築由来で、弱ってきていたことを含意する。
contrastJapanese: shore up は弱った物を支える。build up は時間をかけて強くする。

meaning: Next to each other, or working together.
easyEnglish: Next to each other, or working together.
japanese: 並んで。また、協力し合って。
cue: Describe how two people worked on a task.
reply: They worked side by side for three years.
transferCue: Describe a comparison layout.
transferReply: Put the two versions side by side.
nuance: Fixed word order with no articles. Two senses: physically adjacent, and cooperating.

exampleTranslations.They worked side by side for three years: 二人は3年間、肩を並べて働きました。
2つの版を並べて置いてください。

nuanceJapanese: 冠詞のない固定表現で、語順も変わらない。「隣り合って」と「協力して」の2つの意味がある。

meaning: Be acceptable to someone.
easyEnglish: Be acceptable to someone.
japanese: その人にとって、納得がいく。
cue: A decision has made people uneasy.
reply: The change doesn't sit well with the team.
transferCue: Describe an acceptable compromise.
transferReply: That version sits well with everyone.
nuance: With introduces the person. Very often negative, as a polite way to report discomfort.

exampleTranslations.The change doesn't sit well with the tea: あの変更は、チームには納得がいかないようです。
その案なら、全員が納得しています。

nuanceJapanese: 相手は with で示す。否定形で使うことが非常に多く、不満を穏やかに伝えられる。

meaning: Be missed by a system that should have caught it.
easyEnglish: Be missed by a system that should have caught it.
japanese: 仕組みの網の目から、漏れてしまう。
cue: One case was not picked up by a review.
reply: A few cases slipped through the net last year.
transferCue: Describe improving a process.
transferReply: The new check stops things slipping through the net.
nuance: British; American English says slip through the cracks. It blames the system, not a person.

exampleTranslations.A few cases slipped through the net last: 昨年、いくつかの案件が網から漏れました。
exampleTranslations.The new check stops things slipping thro: 新しい確認で、漏れが起きなくなります。

nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、アメリカ英語では slip through the cracks と言う。人ではなく仕組みの問題を示す。

meaning: Say honestly what you think.
easyEnglish: Say honestly what you think.
japanese: 思っていることを、率直に言う。
cue: A colleague is known for being direct.
reply: She speaks her mind, which I value.
transferCue: Invite honest comment.
transferReply: Please speak your mind — this is a draft.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Usually approving, unlike blunt or tactless.

彼女は率直に意見を言う人で、そこを買っています。
exampleTranslations.Please speak your mind — this is a draft: 率直に言ってください。まだ草案ですから。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。blunt や tactless と違い、ふつうは肯定的。

meaning: Be a sign that problems are coming.
easyEnglish: Be a sign that problems are coming.
japanese: 面倒の前触れになる。
cue: An early warning sign has appeared.
reply: Three cancellations in a week spells trouble.
transferCue: Describe a worrying forecast.
transferReply: Frost in May spells trouble for the fruit.
nuance: Trouble takes no article. The sign is the subject, and for introduces who is affected.

exampleTranslations.Three cancellations in a week spells tro: 1週間に3件の取り消しは、面倒の前触れです。
exampleTranslations.Frost in May spells trouble for the frui: 5月の霜は、果物にとって厄介の前触れです。

nuanceJapanese: trouble に冠詞は付かない。主語は兆候のほうで、影響を受ける側は for で示す。

meaning: Exactly right.
easyEnglish: Exactly right.
japanese: まさにそのとおり。ぴたりと正確。
cue: A colleague's summary captured it exactly.
reply: That summary is spot on.
transferCue: Confirm an accurate measurement.
transferReply: The measurements were spot on.
nuance: British and informal. It follows be or stands alone as a one-word agreement.

その要約は、まさにそのとおりです。
寸法は、ぴたりと正確でした。

nuanceJapanese: くだけたイギリス英語。be のあとに置くか、単独で同意を示す返事として使う。

meaning: Come into your thoughts immediately.
easyEnglish: Come into your thoughts immediately.
japanese: ぱっと頭に浮かぶ。
cue: You are asked for an example without warning.
reply: Two examples spring to mind.
transferCue: Admit you cannot think of one.
transferReply: Nothing springs to mind, I'm afraid.
nuance: Spring is irregular: sprang, sprung. The idea is the subject, and mind takes no article.

ふたつ、すぐに思い浮かびます。
残念ながら、何も思い浮かびません。

nuanceJapanese: spring は不規則変化で sprang、sprung。主語は思いつくもので、mind に冠詞は付かない。

meaning: State publicly that you have a right to something.
easyEnglish: State publicly that you have a right to something.
japanese: 権利があると、はっきり主張する。
cue: Someone put themselves forward for a role early.
reply: She staked a claim to the project in March.
transferCue: Describe competing for territory.
transferReply: Both firms have staked a claim to the market.
nuance: To introduces what is claimed. It implies acting early to secure a position.

exampleTranslations.She staked a claim to the project in Mar: 彼女は3月に、その企画への意欲を明確に示しました。
exampleTranslations.Both firms have staked a claim to the ma: 両社とも、その市場に名乗りを上げています。

nuanceJapanese: 主張の対象は to で示す。先んじて立場を確保する含みがある。

meaning: Accept that you were wrong after being told.
easyEnglish: Accept that you were wrong after being told.
japanese: 指摘を受けて、誤りを認める。
cue: Someone corrects a detail you had wrong.
reply: It was 2018? I stand corrected.
transferCue: Accept a correction in writing.
transferReply: I stand corrected on the figure.
nuance: Almost always first person and present tense. Gracious rather than defensive.

2018年でしたか。訂正します、失礼しました。
その数字については、私の誤りでした。

nuanceJapanese: ほぼつねに一人称の現在形。身構えるのではなく、潔く認める言い方。

meaning: Refuse to change your position under pressure.
easyEnglish: Refuse to change your position under pressure.
japanese: 圧力に屈せず、立場を貫く。
cue: A supplier is pressing for a change of terms.
reply: We should stand firm on the payment schedule.
transferCue: Describe resisting pressure.
transferReply: The committee stood firm despite the letters.
nuance: Stand is irregular: stood. On introduces the issue. Firm is an adverb here, not firmly.

exampleTranslations.We should stand firm on the payment sche: 支払い条件については、譲らないほうがいいでしょう。
exampleTranslations.The committee stood firm despite the let: 多くの手紙が来ても、委員会は姿勢を変えませんでした。

nuanceJapanese: stand は不規則変化で stood。争点は on で示す。ここでの firm は副詞で、firmly とは言わない。

meaning: Behave very formally.
easyEnglish: Behave very formally.
japanese: 堅苦しく、形式ばる。
cue: You want a guest to feel relaxed.
reply: Don't stand on ceremony — help yourself.
transferCue: Describe an informal workplace.
transferReply: Nobody stands on ceremony here.
nuance: Ceremony takes no article. Almost always in the negative, as an invitation to relax.

堅苦しくせず、どうぞご自由に取ってください。
ここでは、誰も堅苦しくしません。

nuanceJapanese: ceremony に冠詞は付かない。ほぼつねに否定形で、くつろぐよう促す表現。

meaning: Remain where you are.
easyEnglish: Remain where you are.
japanese: その場を動かずにいる。
cue: A group is separating in a crowded place.
reply: Stay put and I'll find you.
transferCue: Describe a decision not to move house.
transferReply: We've decided to stay put for another year.
nuance: Put is fixed and does not change. Used for people and for objects that should not move.

そこを動かないでください。私が探します。
exampleTranslations.We've decided to stay put for another ye: もう1年、今の家にとどまることにしました。

nuanceJapanese: put は固定で変化しない。人にも、動かしたくない物にも使う。

meaning: Take responsibility when it is needed.
easyEnglish: Take responsibility when it is needed.
japanese: 必要な場面で、進んで責任を引き受ける。
cue: Someone volunteered when a leader left.
reply: She stepped up to the plate when he resigned.
transferCue: Call for volunteers.
transferReply: We need someone to step up to the plate.
nuance: From baseball, and mostly American. Plate takes the, and the phrase praises initiative.

exampleTranslations.She stepped up to the plate when he resi: 彼が辞任したとき、彼女が進んで役割を引き受けました。
誰かが、進んで引き受けてくれる必要があります。

nuanceJapanese: 野球由来で主にアメリカ英語。plate には the を付け、自発性をほめる表現。

meaning: Almost do something, but not quite.
easyEnglish: Almost do something, but not quite.
japanese: すんでのところで、そこまではしない。
cue: A report criticised without naming anyone.
reply: The review stops short of blaming anyone.
transferCue: Describe a partial apology.
transferReply: He stopped short of apologising properly.
nuance: Followed by -ing. It marks the limit of an action, often with a note of criticism.

exampleTranslations.The review stops short of blaming anyone: その検証は、誰かを名指しするまでには至っていません。
exampleTranslations.He stopped short of apologising properly: 彼はきちんと謝るところまでは行きませんでした。

nuanceJapanese: -ing を続ける。行為の限界を示し、批判を含むことが多い。

meaning: Reach an agreement after negotiating.
easyEnglish: Reach an agreement after negotiating.
japanese: 交渉の末に、取引をまとめる。
cue: Two sides agreed after a long discussion.
reply: They struck a deal late on Friday.
transferCue: Describe negotiating at a market.
transferReply: We struck a deal at half the asking price.
nuance: Strike is irregular: struck. With introduces the other party.

金曜の遅くに、双方は取引をまとめました。
exampleTranslations.We struck a deal at half the asking pric: 言い値の半額で、話をまとめました。

nuanceJapanese: strike は不規則変化で struck。相手は with で示す。

phrase: strike while the iron is hot
meaning: Act now, while conditions are favourable.
easyEnglish: Act now, while conditions are favourable.
japanese: 好機のうちに、すぐ動く。
cue: Interest in a proposal is high right now.
reply: Let's strike while the iron is hot and send it today.
transferCue: Describe acting on an offer.
transferReply: She struck while the iron was hot and accepted.
frame: Strike while the iron is hot
nuance: From blacksmithing. The tense of is follows the sentence, as in while the iron was hot.
aliases: strike while the iron was hot

exampleTranslations.Let's strike while the iron is hot and s: 好機のうちに、今日中に送ってしまいましょう。
exampleTranslations.She struck while the iron was hot and ac: 彼女は好機を逃さず、その場で受けました。

nuanceJapanese: 鍛冶に由来。is の時制は文に合わせ、while the iron was hot のようになる。
pronunciation: straɪk waɪl ði ˈaɪɚn ɪz hɑːt

meaning: The obstacle that prevents progress.
easyEnglish: The obstacle that prevents progress.
japanese: 前に進むのを妨げている、障害。
cue: One issue is holding up an agreement.
reply: Price is the main stumbling block.
transferCue: Describe an obstacle in learning.
transferReply: Pronunciation was a stumbling block at first.
nuance: Countable. It names the single obstacle in the way, not general difficulty.

最大の障害は、価格です。
exampleTranslations.Pronunciation was a stumbling block at f: 最初は、発音が壁になりました。

nuanceJapanese: 可算名詞。漠然とした困難ではなく、行く手をふさぐ具体的な障害を指す。

meaning: Do the opposite of what most people are doing.
easyEnglish: Do the opposite of what most people are doing.
japanese: 大勢の流れに、逆らって進む。
cue: Someone holds an unpopular position.
reply: She's swimming against the tide on this one.
transferCue: Describe a business resisting a trend.
transferReply: The shop swims against the tide and still thrives.
nuance: Swim is irregular: swam, swum. Tide takes the, and the phrase implies effort, not error.

exampleTranslations.She's swimming against the tide on this: この件で、彼女は流れに逆らっています。
exampleTranslations.The shop swims against the tide and stil: あの店は流れに逆らいながら、今も繁盛しています。

nuanceJapanese: swim は不規則変化で swam、swum。tide には the を付け、誤りではなく労力を含意する。

meaning: Adopt a strict position and refuse to soften it.
easyEnglish: Adopt a strict position and refuse to soften it.
japanese: 強硬な姿勢を取って、譲らない。
cue: An organisation refuses to negotiate on a point.
reply: They take a hard line on late payment.
transferCue: Describe a softer approach.
transferReply: We'd rather not take a hard line yet.
frame: Take a hard line on something
nuance: On introduces the issue. Line takes a. It describes policy, not anger.

支払い遅延について、彼らは強硬な姿勢です。
今はまだ、強硬な姿勢は取りたくありません。

nuanceJapanese: 争点は on で示す。line には a を付ける。怒りではなく、方針についての表現。

meaning: Start liking someone quickly.
easyEnglish: Start liking someone quickly.
japanese: すぐに、その人を気に入る。
cue: A normally reserved colleague warmed to a newcomer.
reply: He's taken a shine to the new apprentice.
transferCue: Describe a cat and a visitor.
transferReply: The cat took a shine to her immediately.
nuance: Informal and warm. To introduces the person, and it implies the liking was quick.

exampleTranslations.He's taken a shine to the new apprentice: 彼は新しい見習いを、すっかり気に入ったようです。
猫はすぐに、彼女になつきました。

nuanceJapanese: くだけた温かい表現。相手は to で示し、すぐに好きになったことを含意する。

meaning: Move somewhere safe from danger or weather.
easyEnglish: Move somewhere safe from danger or weather.
japanese: 危険や雨風から、身を隠す。
cue: A sudden downpour began on a walk.
reply: We took cover under a tree.
transferCue: Describe a warning at a site.
transferReply: Take cover when you hear the siren.
nuance: Cover takes no article. Used for weather and for danger alike.

木の下で、雨宿りしました。
サイレンが鳴ったら、安全な場所に避難してください。

nuanceJapanese: cover に冠詞は付かない。天候にも危険にも使う。

meaning: Feel encouraged by something.
easyEnglish: Feel encouraged by something.
japanese: それを励みにして、気を取り直す。
cue: A difficult period has one positive sign.
reply: We can take heart from the March figures.
transferCue: Encourage a friend after a setback.
transferReply: Take heart — the second attempt is always easier.
nuance: Heart takes no article. From introduces the encouraging thing. The opposite is lose heart.

exampleTranslations.We can take heart from the March figures: 3月の数字を、励みにできます。
exampleTranslations.Take heart — the second attempt is alway: 気を落とさないで。2回目はいつも楽になります。

nuanceJapanese: heart に冠詞は付かない。励みになるものは from で示す。反対は lose heart。

meaning: Make a careful effort to do something well.
easyEnglish: Make a careful effort to do something well.
japanese: 手間を惜しまず、丁寧にやる。
cue: Someone was unusually careful in their explanation.
reply: She took pains to explain it clearly.
transferCue: Describe careful craftsmanship.
transferReply: He takes pains over every joint.
nuance: Pains is always plural. To plus a verb, or over plus a noun, introduces the care taken.

彼女は手間を惜しまず、丁寧に説明してくれました。
彼はどの継ぎ目にも、丁寧に手をかけます。

nuanceJapanese: pains はつねに複数形。to＋動詞、または over＋名詞で、丁寧にする対象を示す。

meaning: Gradually develop into a recognisable form.
easyEnglish: Gradually develop into a recognisable form.
japanese: だんだん、形になってくる。
cue: A plan is becoming clearer.
reply: The proposal is starting to take shape.
transferCue: Describe a building under construction.
transferReply: The extension is taking shape nicely.
nuance: Shape takes no article. Usually in the continuous, since it describes gradual progress.

提案が、少しずつ形になってきました。
増築部分が、うまく形になってきています。

nuanceJapanese: shape に冠詞は付かない。徐々に進む様子を表すので、ふつう進行形で使う。

meaning: Support one person or group in an argument.
easyEnglish: Support one person or group in an argument.
japanese: どちらか一方の側につく。
cue: Two friends have fallen out and both want support.
reply: I'd rather not take sides in this.
transferCue: Describe a neutral chair.
transferReply: A good chair doesn't take sides.
nuance: Sides is always plural, even when supporting one. In introduces the dispute.

この件では、どちらの味方にもなりたくありません。
よい議長は、どちらにも肩入れしません。

nuanceJapanese: 一方につく場合でも sides はつねに複数形。争いは in で示す。

meaning: Criticise someone firmly for something they did.
easyEnglish: Criticise someone firmly for something they did.
japanese: その行いについて、厳しく咎める。
cue: A manager addressed a repeated failure directly.
reply: She took him to task over the missing reports.
transferCue: Describe a critical review.
transferReply: The article takes the council to task for the delay.
frame: Take someone to task over something
nuance: The person goes between take and to. Over or for introduces the fault. Formal in tone.

exampleTranslations.She took him to task over the missing re: 彼女は報告書の不備について、彼を厳しく咎めました。
exampleTranslations.The article takes the council to task fo: その記事は、遅延について自治体を厳しく批判しています。

nuanceJapanese: 相手は take と to のあいだに置く。理由は over か for で示す。改まった響き。

meaning: The less bad of two poor options.
easyEnglish: The less bad of two poor options.
japanese: どちらも悪いなかで、まだましなほう。
cue: Neither available option is good. Choose anyway.
reply: Waiting is the lesser of two evils.
transferCue: Describe an unwelcome compromise.
transferReply: We took the lesser of two evils and paid the fee.
nuance: Fixed with the and two. It accepts that neither option is good.

待つほうが、まだましです。
exampleTranslations.We took the lesser of two evils and paid: まだましなほうを選んで、手数料を払いました。

nuanceJapanese: the と two を含む固定表現。どちらもよくないことを前提とする。

meaning: The point when you find out whether something works.
easyEnglish: The point when you find out whether something works.
japanese: 結果が分かる、決定的な瞬間。
cue: A repair is about to be tested.
reply: This is the moment of truth — try the switch.
transferCue: Describe opening exam results.
transferReply: The moment of truth came with the envelope.
nuance: Always with the. It names a single decisive instant, often with light drama.

exampleTranslations.This is the moment of truth — try the sw: いよいよ本番です。スイッチを入れてみてください。
exampleTranslations.The moment of truth came with the envelo: 封筒を開けるときが、決定的な瞬間でした。

nuanceJapanese: つねに the を伴う。決定的な一瞬を指し、やや芝居がかった響きになる。

meaning: What is usual or expected in a situation.
easyEnglish: What is usual or expected in a situation.
japanese: その場では、当たり前になっていること。
cue: Describe the atmosphere during a busy period.
reply: Long hours were the order of the day that month.
transferCue: Describe a relaxed dress code.
transferReply: Jeans are the order of the day here.
frame: Be the order of the day
nuance: Always with the. It describes what prevails, not a formal rule.

exampleTranslations.Long hours were the order of the day tha: あの月は、長時間労働が当たり前でした。
ここでは、ジーンズが当たり前です。

nuanceJapanese: つねに the を伴う。正式な規則ではなく、実際に行き渡っている状態を表す。

meaning: The advantages and disadvantages.
easyEnglish: The advantages and disadvantages.
japanese: 利点と欠点の両方。
cue: A decision needs weighing up.
reply: Let's list the pros and cons before Friday.
transferCue: Describe a balanced discussion.
transferReply: We went through the pros and cons twice.
frame: Weigh up the pros and cons
nuance: Both words are always plural and in that order. They are short for Latin pro and contra.

exampleTranslations.Let's list the pros and cons before Frid: 金曜までに、利点と欠点を挙げてみましょう。
利点と欠点を、2回検討しました。

nuanceJapanese: どちらもつねに複数形で、語順も固定。ラテン語の pro と contra に由来する。

meaning: Fit together with something else.
easyEnglish: Fit together with something else.
japanese: ほかのものと、うまくつながる。
cue: A new finding matches an earlier one.
reply: That ties in with what the survey found.
transferCue: Describe coordinating two events.
transferReply: The launch ties in with the anniversary.
nuance: Inseparable. Used for evidence that agrees and for events timed together.
contrast: Tie in with fits an existing thing; lead to produces it.

それは、調査で分かったこととつながります。
発表は、記念日に合わせてあります。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。一致する証拠にも、時期を合わせた催しにも使う。
contrastJapanese: tie in with は既存のものと噛み合う。lead to はそれを生み出す。

meaning: Repeatedly, on many occasions.
easyEnglish: Repeatedly, on many occasions.
japanese: 何度となく、繰り返し。
cue: A warning has been given many times.
reply: We've said this time and again.
transferCue: Describe a proven method.
transferReply: It has worked time and again.
nuance: Often extended to time and time again. It usually carries mild frustration or emphasis.

このことは、何度となく言ってきました。
その方法は、何度も効果を上げてきました。

nuanceJapanese: time and time again と長くすることも多い。軽いいらだちや強調を伴うことが多い。

meaning: Without achieving anything.
easyEnglish: Without achieving anything.
japanese: 何の効果もなく。むだに終わって。
cue: Repeated attempts produced no result.
reply: We called three times, to no avail.
transferCue: Describe a failed search.
transferReply: They searched all evening, to no avail.
nuance: Formal, usually at the end after a comma. Avail takes no article.

3回電話しましたが、むだでした。
一晩中探しましたが、見つかりませんでした。

nuanceJapanese: 改まった表現で、ふつう文末にコンマを添えて置く。avail に冠詞は付かない。

meaning: Confronting each other directly as equals.
easyEnglish: Confronting each other directly as equals.
japanese: 真っ向から、対等に渡り合って。
cue: A small firm competed evenly with a large one.
reply: They went toe to toe with a much bigger rival.
transferCue: Describe a close debate.
transferReply: The two candidates stood toe to toe all evening.
frame: Go toe to toe with someone
nuance: From boxing. With introduces the opponent, and it implies the sides were evenly matched.

exampleTranslations.They went toe to toe with a much bigger: 彼らははるかに大きい相手と、対等に渡り合いました。
exampleTranslations.The two candidates stood toe to toe all: 二人の候補は一晩中、真っ向から渡り合いました。

nuanceJapanese: ボクシング由来。相手は with で示し、互角であったことを含意する。

meaning: Endure a difficult situation rather than giving up.
easyEnglish: Endure a difficult situation rather than giving up.
japanese: 投げ出さずに、耐え抜く。
cue: A hard period has a few weeks left.
reply: We'll tough it out until the end of term.
transferCue: Describe finishing a race while injured.
transferReply: She toughed it out and finished.
nuance: Fixed with it. Informal, and it emphasises endurance rather than solving the problem.

exampleTranslations.We'll tough it out until the end of term: 学期末まで、耐え抜きましょう。
彼女は耐え抜いて、完走しました。

nuanceJapanese: it を伴う固定表現。くだけた言い方で、解決ではなく耐えることを強調する。

meaning: Locked away securely.
easyEnglish: Locked away securely.
japanese: 厳重に鍵をかけて、しまってある。
cue: Sensitive documents need secure storage.
reply: The originals are under lock and key.
transferCue: Describe keeping something safe at home.
transferReply: The spare keys stay under lock and key.
frame: Keep something under lock and key
nuance: Fixed word order with no articles. It emphasises security more than simply being locked.

原本は、厳重に保管してあります。
予備の鍵は、厳重にしまってあります。

nuanceJapanese: 冠詞のない固定表現で、語順も変わらない。単に施錠する以上の厳重さを示す。

meaning: Paid or stated in advance, or open and direct.
easyEnglish: Paid or stated in advance, or open and direct.
japanese: 前払いで。また、隠さず率直に。
cue: Explain a payment arrangement.
reply: They want half the fee up front.
transferCue: Describe honest communication.
transferReply: She was up front about the risks.
frame: Pay up front / be up front about something
nuance: Written as one word or two. Two senses: paid in advance, and honest about something.

先方は、料金の半額を前払いで求めています。
彼女は危険について、隠さず話してくれました。

nuanceJapanese: 1語でも2語でも書く。「前払い」と「率直」の2つの意味がある。

meaning: Manage carefully between two opposing risks.
easyEnglish: Manage carefully between two opposing risks.
japanese: 両方の危うさのあいだで、慎重に進む。
cue: A policy must be firm but not harsh.
reply: We walk a fine line between clear and unkind.
transferCue: Describe a comedian's material.
transferReply: He walks a fine line and usually gets it right.
frame: Walk a fine line between two things
nuance: Between introduces the two risks. Tread a fine line means the same in British English.

exampleTranslations.We walk a fine line between clear and un: 明確さと冷たさのあいだで、慎重に線を引いています。
exampleTranslations.He walks a fine line and usually gets it: 彼は際どい線を歩きますが、たいていは外しません。

nuanceJapanese: 2つの危うさは between で示す。イギリス英語では tread a fine line とも言う。

meaning: Actually do what you have said you would do.
easyEnglish: Actually do what you have said you would do.
japanese: 口だけでなく、実際に行動する。
cue: Someone's actions matched their stated values.
reply: He talks the talk and walks the walk.
transferCue: Question an organisation's claims.
transferReply: They say the right things, but do they walk the walk?
nuance: Usually paired with talk the talk. Informal and mostly American in origin.

彼は口にするだけでなく、実際に行動しています。
exampleTranslations.They say the right things, but do they w: 言うことは立派ですが、実際に行動しているでしょうか。

nuanceJapanese: ふつう talk the talk と対にして使う。くだけた、もとはアメリカ英語の表現。

meaning: Lose something and accept it is gone.
easyEnglish: Lose something and accept it is gone.
japanese: もう戻らないものとして、あきらめる。
cue: A missed deadline lost an opportunity.
reply: We can wave goodbye to the spring slot.
transferCue: Describe losing a deposit.
transferReply: They waved goodbye to the deposit.
nuance: To introduces what is lost. It treats the loss as final, usually with resignation.

春の枠は、あきらめるしかありません。
彼らは手付金をあきらめました。

nuanceJapanese: 失うものは to で示す。取り返しがつかないものとして、あきらめ気味に使う。

meaning: Cause someone serious and continuing worry.
easyEnglish: Cause someone serious and continuing worry.
japanese: 重くのしかかって、悩ませ続ける。
cue: A difficult decision is troubling someone.
reply: The choice weighs heavily on her.
transferCue: Describe responsibility.
transferReply: The responsibility weighed heavily on the whole team.
nuance: The worry is the subject, and on introduces the person. It describes lasting burden.

その選択が、彼女に重くのしかかっています。
exampleTranslations.The responsibility weighed heavily on th: その責任は、チーム全体に重くのしかかりました。

nuanceJapanese: 主語は悩みのほうで、人は on で示す。一時的ではなく、続く重荷を表す。

meaning: Having plenty of money, or in a good situation.
easyEnglish: Having plenty of money, or in a good situation.
japanese: 暮らし向きがよい。恵まれている。
cue: Compare two neighbourhoods.
reply: That part of town is noticeably well off.
transferCue: Point out a hidden advantage.
transferReply: We don't know how well off we are.
nuance: Hyphenated before a noun. Not know when you are well off means failing to see your advantages.

exampleTranslations.That part of town is noticeably well off: 町のあのあたりは、明らかに裕福です。
自分たちがどれだけ恵まれているか、分かっていません。

nuanceJapanese: 名詞の前ではハイフンでつなぐ。not know when you are well off は、恵まれていると気づかないこと。

meaning: Young and without experience.
easyEnglish: Young and without experience.
japanese: 経験が浅く、まだ青い。
cue: Describe yourself at the start of a career.
reply: I was wet behind the ears when I started here.
transferCue: Describe a young colleague fairly.
transferReply: He's a little wet behind the ears but he learns fast.
nuance: Ears is always plural. Mildly critical, so it is gentler about yourself than about others.

exampleTranslations.I was wet behind the ears when I started: ここで働き始めたころは、まだ青二才でした。
exampleTranslations.He's a little wet behind the ears but he: 彼はまだ経験が浅いですが、覚えるのは早いです。

nuanceJapanese: ears はつねに複数形。やや批判的なので、他人より自分について使うほうがやわらかい。

meaning: Get something or someone back after losing them.
easyEnglish: Get something or someone back after losing them.
japanese: 一度失ったものを、取り戻す。
cue: A customer who left has returned.
reply: We won back two of the accounts.
transferCue: Describe rebuilding trust.
transferReply: It took a year to win back their confidence.
nuance: Separable: win it back. Win is irregular: won. It implies the loss came first.
contrast: Win back recovers what you lost; take back can mean retracting words.

取引先のうち2社を、取り戻しました。
exampleTranslations.It took a year to win back their confide: 信頼を取り戻すまでに、1年かかりました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：win it back。win は不規則変化で won。まず失ったことが前提になる。
contrastJapanese: win back は失ったものを取り戻す。take back は発言の撤回にも使う。

meaning: Very warmly and willingly.
easyEnglish: Very warmly and willingly.
japanese: 両手を広げて、心から歓迎して。
cue: A returning colleague was warmly received.
reply: The team welcomed her back with open arms.
transferCue: Describe accepting an idea.
transferReply: The idea was received with open arms.
nuance: Arms is always plural. Usually with welcome or receive, and always positive.

exampleTranslations.The team welcomed her back with open arm: チームは彼女を、心から歓迎して迎えました。
その案は、両手を広げて受け入れられました。

nuanceJapanese: arms はつねに複数形。welcome や receive と使い、つねに肯定的。

meaning: Reach a senior position by starting at the bottom.
easyEnglish: Reach a senior position by starting at the bottom.
japanese: 下から始めて、階段を上っていく。
cue: Describe a colleague's career path.
reply: She worked her way up from the post room.
transferCue: Describe an expectation in a trade.
transferReply: Most people work their way up over ten years.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. It implies slow progress earned by effort.

exampleTranslations.She worked her way up from the post room: 彼女は郵便室から始めて、今の立場に上がりました。
exampleTranslations.Most people work their way up over ten y: たいていの人は、10年かけて上がっていきます。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。努力で少しずつ上がることを含意する。

meaning: Manage to understand something difficult.
easyEnglish: Manage to understand something difficult.
japanese: 難しいことを、なんとかのみこむ。
cue: A new concept is hard to grasp.
reply: I can't quite wrap my mind around the pricing.
transferCue: Describe absorbing surprising news.
transferReply: It takes a while to wrap your mind around it.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Head is the more common variant; both are informal.

exampleTranslations.I can't quite wrap my mind around the pr: あの料金体系が、どうにものみこめません。
exampleTranslations.It takes a while to wrap your mind aroun: のみこむまでに、しばらくかかります。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。head を使う形のほうが一般的で、どちらもくだけた表現。

meaning: Not important at all.
easyEnglish: Not important at all.
japanese: 取るに足らず、重要ではない。
cue: A small discrepancy does not affect anything.
reply: A day either way is of no consequence.
transferCue: Dismiss a minor objection.
transferReply: The colour is of no consequence here.
nuance: Formal. Consequence takes no article in this sense, and the phrase follows be.

1日ずれても、大した問題ではありません。
ここでは、色は問題になりません。

nuanceJapanese: 改まった表現。この意味では consequence に冠詞は付かず、be のあとに置く。

meaning: Deeply asleep or unconscious.
easyEnglish: Deeply asleep or unconscious.
japanese: ぐっすり眠り込んでいる。
cue: Describe a child after a long day out.
reply: He was out for the count by seven.
transferCue: Describe yourself after a long journey.
transferReply: I was out for the count within minutes.
nuance: From boxing. British and informal, and usually about deep sleep rather than injury.

彼は7時には、ぐっすり眠っていました。
数分で、私は眠り込んでいました。

nuanceJapanese: ボクシング由来のくだけたイギリス英語。けがではなく、深い眠りについて使う。

meaning: Not something that affects or bothers me.
easyEnglish: Not something that affects or bothers me.
japanese: 自分には、痛くもかゆくもない。
cue: A change does not affect you either way.
reply: It's no skin off my nose which room we use.
transferCue: Decline to object to a plan.
transferReply: Go ahead — no skin off my nose.
frame: Be no skin off my nose
nuance: Informal, and the possessive follows the speaker. It can sound indifferent, so tone matters.

exampleTranslations.It's no skin off my nose which room we u: どちらの部屋でも、私は構いません。
どうぞ進めてください。私には関係ありません。

nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現で、所有格は話し手に合わせる。冷たく響くこともあるので、口調に注意。

meaning: Gain an advantage by acting before others.
easyEnglish: Gain an advantage by acting before others.
japanese: 先手を打って、優位に立つ。
cue: A competitor launched first.
reply: They stole a march on us with the early launch.
transferCue: Describe acting first yourself.
transferReply: We stole a march by booking in January.
nuance: Steal is irregular: stole, stolen. On introduces the rival who was beaten to it.

exampleTranslations.They stole a march on us with the early: 先行発売で、彼らに先を越されました。
1月に予約して、先手を打ちました。

nuanceJapanese: steal は不規則変化で stole、stolen。先を越された相手は on で示す。

meaning: People or things that are not important compared with others.
easyEnglish: People or things that are not important compared with others.
japanese: ほかと比べれば、取るに足りない存在。
cue: A minor case sits alongside much larger ones.
reply: Our order is small fry to a supplier that size.
transferCue: Describe a minor player in a market.
transferReply: They were small fry until the merger.
nuance: Uncountable and always plural in form. It compares, so it needs a larger thing in view.

exampleTranslations.Our order is small fry to a supplier tha: あの規模の業者にとって、うちの注文は小さなものです。
合併までは、彼らは小さな存在でした。

nuanceJapanese: 不可算だが形はつねに複数。比較の表現なので、より大きな対象が前提になる。

meaning: Dismiss an objection without properly considering it.
easyEnglish: Dismiss an objection without properly considering it.
japanese: 異論を、まともに取り合わずに退ける。
cue: Concerns were raised and ignored.
reply: They swept aside every objection.
transferCue: Describe removing an obstacle easily.
transferReply: The new evidence swept aside the old theory.
nuance: Separable: sweep it aside. Sweep is irregular: swept. Usually critical when used about objections.
contrast: Sweep aside dismisses without considering; brush aside is the same act, slightly milder.

彼らはすべての異論を、退けてしまいました。
exampleTranslations.The new evidence swept aside the old the: 新しい証拠が、古い説を一掃しました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：sweep it aside。sweep は不規則変化で swept。異論について使うと批判的になる。
contrastJapanese: sweep aside は検討せず退ける。brush aside は同じ行為でやや穏やか。

meaning: Say things that are reasonable and practical.
easyEnglish: Say things that are reasonable and practical.
japanese: 筋の通った、現実的なことを言う。
cue: One person brought a discussion back to reality.
reply: At last, somebody talking sense.
transferCue: Ask someone to be realistic.
transferReply: Talk sense — we can't do it in a day.
nuance: Sense takes no article. As a command it is blunt, so it suits close colleagues.

やっと、まともなことを言う人が出ました。
現実的に考えてください。1日では無理です。

nuanceJapanese: sense に冠詞は付かない。命令形はぶっきらぼうなので、親しい相手向き。

meaning: Revealing something that was meant to be hidden.
easyEnglish: Revealing something that was meant to be hidden.
japanese: 隠していたことを、うっかり示してしまう。
cue: Small signs revealed that someone had been in a room.
reply: There were tell-tale crumbs on the desk.
transferCue: Describe symptoms of a fault.
transferReply: The tell-tale rattle started again.
nuance: Hyphenated and used before a noun. Very often with sign or signs.

机の上に、それと分かるパンくずが残っていました。
例のがたつく音が、また始まりました。

nuanceJapanese: ハイフンでつなぎ、名詞の前に置く。sign や signs と組み合わせることが非常に多い。

meaning: Earn a very large amount of money.
easyEnglish: Earn a very large amount of money.
japanese: 大金をどんどん稼ぐ。
cue: A popular stall sold out every day. Describe it.
reply: They were raking in money all weekend.
transferCue: Describe a successful film.
transferReply: The sequel raked in twice as much.
nuance: Separable: rake it in. Informal, and it can imply the earnings are effortless or excessive.
contrast: Rake in stresses the amount earned; make a killing stresses how quickly it happened.

あの週末、彼らは大金を稼いでいました。
続編は、2倍の興行収入を上げました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：rake it in。くだけた表現で、楽に、あるいは度を越して稼ぐ含みが出ることがある。
contrastJapanese: rake in は稼ぐ額を強調する。make a killing は短期間であることを強調する。

meaning: Increase something quickly and deliberately.
easyEnglish: Increase something quickly and deliberately.
japanese: 意図して、一気に増やす。
cue: Production must rise before a busy season.
reply: We ramp up production in October.
transferCue: Describe increasing effort.
transferReply: They ramped up the advertising before the launch.
nuance: Separable: ramp it up. It implies a planned increase over a period, not a single jump.
contrast: Ramp up builds gradually to a higher level; bump up is a single step increase.

10月から、生産を一気に増やします。
exampleTranslations.They ramped up the advertising before th: 発売前に、彼らは広告を大幅に増やしました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：ramp it up。一度の跳ね上がりではなく、期間をかけた計画的な増加を含意する。
contrastJapanese: ramp up は段階的に水準を上げる。bump up は一段階だけ上げる。

meaning: Tell someone in authority about what another person did.
easyEnglish: Tell someone in authority about what another person did.
japanese: 仲間のことを、上に告げ口する。
cue: Someone reported a colleague's shortcut.
reply: Nobody wants to rat on a workmate.
transferCue: Describe a broken promise.
transferReply: He ratted on the deal they had agreed.
nuance: Inseparable and informal, with a strong note of disloyalty. Inform on is the neutral word.
contrast: Rat on implies betraying a peer; inform on is neutral about reporting wrongdoing.

同僚を告げ口したい人など、いません。
彼は、二人で決めた約束を破りました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できないくだけた表現で、裏切りの含みが強い。中立的には inform on を使う。
contrastJapanese: rat on は仲間を裏切る含み。inform on は中立に不正を通報すること。

meaning: Contact someone, often to offer or ask for help.
easyEnglish: Contact someone, often to offer or ask for help.
japanese: 連絡を取る。手を差し伸べる。
cue: A colleague has been quiet for weeks.
reply: I'll reach out to her this week.
transferCue: Describe a support service.
transferReply: The charity reaches out to families in the area.
nuance: Inseparable. Common in supportive and professional contexts; contact is more neutral.
contrast: Reach out to initiates contact warmly; get in touch with is plainer.

今週、彼女に連絡を取ってみます。
exampleTranslations.The charity reaches out to families in t: その団体は、地域の家庭に手を差し伸べています。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。支援や仕事の文脈でよく使う。より中立なのは contact。
contrastJapanese: reach out to は温かく連絡を取る。get in touch with はより素っ気ない。

meaning: Take something seriously into account.
easyEnglish: Take something seriously into account.
japanese: 無視できないものとして、考慮に入れる。
cue: A factor cannot be ignored in planning.
reply: We have to reckon with the winter closures.
transferCue: Describe a formidable competitor.
transferReply: They're a force to be reckoned with now.
nuance: Inseparable. A force to be reckoned with is a common fixed phrase built on it.
contrast: Reckon with takes a factor seriously; allow for builds margin into a plan.

exampleTranslations.We have to reckon with the winter closur: 冬の閉鎖を、計算に入れる必要があります。
彼らは今や、侮れない存在です。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。a force to be reckoned with という決まった言い方がよく使われる。
contrastJapanese: reckon with は要因を重く見る。allow for は計画に余裕を持たせる。

meaning: Think carefully about something that has happened.
easyEnglish: Think carefully about something that has happened.
japanese: 起きたことを、じっくり振り返る。
cue: A project has ended and lessons remain.
reply: Let's reflect on what worked before we plan again.
transferCue: Describe writing a diary.
transferReply: She reflects on the day for ten minutes each night.
nuance: Inseparable. Reflect on someone also means affecting how people judge them.
contrast: Reflect on reviews the past; think through follows consequences forward.

exampleTranslations.Let's reflect on what worked before we p: 次の計画の前に、うまくいった点を振り返りましょう。
exampleTranslations.She reflects on the day for ten minutes: 彼女は毎晩10分、その日を振り返ります。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。reflect on someone なら「その人の評価に影響する」という意味にもなる。
contrastJapanese: reflect on は過去を振り返る。think through は先の結果を追う。

meaning: Return with information after doing something.
easyEnglish: Return with information after doing something.
japanese: 結果を、あとから報告する。
cue: Someone is investigating and will inform the group.
reply: I'll report back after the site visit.
transferCue: Describe a working group.
transferReply: The panel reports back in June.
nuance: Intransitive; on introduces the subject and to introduces the audience.
contrast: Report back returns with findings; follow up returns to an earlier contact.

現地訪問のあと、ご報告します。
その部会は、6月に報告します。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、報告内容は on、報告先は to で示す。
contrastJapanese: report back は調べた結果を持ち帰る。follow up は前のやり取りに戻る。

meaning: Cause a particular outcome.
easyEnglish: Cause a particular outcome.
japanese: その結果を、もたらす。
cue: A change had a clear consequence.
reply: The new route resulted in fewer delays.
transferCue: Describe a failed process.
transferReply: The error resulted in two weeks of rework.
nuance: Inseparable and slightly formal. Result from reverses the direction: it names the cause.
contrast: Result in names the outcome; result from names the cause.

新しい経路によって、遅延が減りました。
exampleTranslations.The error resulted in two weeks of rewor: その誤りが、2週間の手戻りを招きました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない、やや改まった表現。result from なら向きが逆で、原因を示す。
contrastJapanese: result in は結果を示す。result from は原因を示す。

meaning: Return to a previous state or way of doing things.
easyEnglish: Return to a previous state or way of doing things.
japanese: 以前の状態やり方に、戻る。
cue: A trial was abandoned and the old method returned.
reply: We reverted to the old form in March.
transferCue: Describe a habit returning.
transferReply: He reverted to type within a week.
nuance: Inseparable and slightly formal. Revert to type means returning to your usual character.
contrast: Revert to returns to a former state; fall back on uses something as a last resort.

3月に、以前の書式に戻しました。
1週間で、彼は元の調子に戻りました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない、やや改まった表現。revert to type は「地が出る」という意味。
contrastJapanese: revert to は以前の状態に戻る。fall back on は最後の手段として頼る。

meaning: Have something as the central concern.
easyEnglish: Have something as the central concern.
japanese: それを中心に、すべてが回っている。
cue: One issue dominates every discussion.
reply: Every meeting revolves around the budget.
transferCue: Describe a family routine.
transferReply: Their week revolves around the children's schedule.
nuance: Inseparable. Stronger than centre on: it implies everything else depends on the centre.
contrast: Revolve around makes something the centre; centre on simply names the main topic.

exampleTranslations.Every meeting revolves around the budget: どの会議も、予算を中心に回っています。
exampleTranslations.Their week revolves around the children': 彼らの一週間は、子どもの予定を中心に回っています。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。centre on より強く、ほかがすべてそれ次第であることを含意する。
contrastJapanese: revolve around は中心として everything を従える。centre on は主題を示すだけ。

meaning: Criticise someone very harshly.
easyEnglish: Criticise someone very harshly.
japanese: 激しく、こき下ろす。
cue: A review was unusually savage.
reply: The critic ripped into the second act.
transferCue: Describe a heated meeting.
transferReply: He ripped into the proposal without reading it.
nuance: Inseparable and informal. Stronger than criticise, and it implies loss of restraint.
contrast: Rip into is harsh public criticism; take to task is firmer but more controlled.

その批評家は、第2幕を激しくこき下ろしました。
exampleTranslations.He ripped into the proposal without read: 彼は読みもせず、その提案をこき下ろしました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できないくだけた表現。criticise より強く、抑制を欠いた響きになる。
contrastJapanese: rip into は激しい批判。take to task は厳しいが抑制の効いた叱責。

meaning: Reverse a change and return to how things were.
easyEnglish: Reverse a change and return to how things were.
japanese: 変更を取り消して、元に戻す。
cue: An update caused problems and was reversed.
reply: We rolled back the change within an hour.
transferCue: Describe reversing a policy.
transferReply: The council rolled back the parking charges.
nuance: Separable: roll it back. Common in technology and in policy.
contrast: Roll back reverses a change; revert to returns to a former state more generally.

exampleTranslations.We rolled back the change within an hour: 1時間以内に、その変更を元に戻しました。
exampleTranslations.The council rolled back the parking char: 自治体は、駐車料金の変更を撤回しました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：roll it back。技術や政策の分野でよく使う。
contrastJapanese: roll back は変更を取り消す。revert to はより一般に以前の状態へ戻る。

meaning: Find and remove something bad completely.
easyEnglish: Find and remove something bad completely.
japanese: 根本から見つけ出して、取り除く。
cue: A recurring fault needs to be eliminated.
reply: We need to root out the cause, not patch it.
transferCue: Describe removing bad practice.
transferReply: The review rooted out three outdated rules.
nuance: Separable: root it out. It implies removing the source, not just the symptom.
contrast: Root out removes the source; stamp out suppresses something already spreading.

exampleTranslations.We need to root out the cause, not patch: 応急処置ではなく、原因を根本から取り除く必要があります。
exampleTranslations.The review rooted out three outdated rul: その見直しで、時代遅れの規則が3つ取り除かれました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：root it out。症状ではなく、原因そのものを除くことを含意する。
contrastJapanese: root out は根源を除く。stamp out は広がりつつあるものを抑え込む。

meaning: Persuade someone to join something they did not want to.
easyEnglish: Persuade someone to join something they did not want to.
japanese: 気の進まない相手を、引っ張り込む。
cue: You ended up helping at an event unexpectedly.
reply: I got roped into running the raffle.
transferCue: Describe recruiting a reluctant helper.
transferReply: She roped her brother into driving.
nuance: The person goes between rope and into. Very often passive: get roped into.
contrast: Rope into recruits the reluctant; talk into persuades by argument.

くじ引きの担当に、引っ張り込まれました。
彼女は弟を、運転役に引っ張り込みました。

nuanceJapanese: 相手は rope と into のあいだに置く。get roped into の受け身が非常に多い。
contrastJapanese: rope into は気の進まない人を巻き込む。talk into は説得して納得させる。

meaning: Make a first, unfinished version of something.
easyEnglish: Make a first, unfinished version of something.
japanese: おおまかな下書きを作る。
cue: A plan needs a first sketch before detail.
reply: I'll rough out the layout this afternoon.
transferCue: Describe an early drawing.
transferReply: She roughed out three designs in an hour.
nuance: Separable: rough it out. It accepts that the version is unfinished by design.
contrast: Rough out makes a first sketch; flesh out adds the missing detail to it.

exampleTranslations.I'll rough out the layout this afternoon: 午後に、レイアウトの概略を作ります。
exampleTranslations.She roughed out three designs in an hour: 彼女は1時間で、3案の概略を描きました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：rough it out。未完成であることを、前提として認める表現。
contrastJapanese: rough out は概略を作る。flesh out はそこに細部を足す。

meaning: Suddenly turn and attack someone verbally.
easyEnglish: Suddenly turn and attack someone verbally.
japanese: 急に矛先を変えて、食ってかかる。
cue: Someone unexpectedly criticised a colleague mid-meeting.
reply: He rounded on her without warning.
transferCue: Describe a crowd reacting.
transferReply: The audience rounded on the speaker.
nuance: Inseparable and British. It stresses the suddenness of the turn, not just the criticism.
contrast: Round on is a sudden verbal attack; lay into is sustained and heavy.

彼は突然、彼女に食ってかかりました。
聴衆は、講演者に一斉に反発しました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できないイギリス英語。批判そのものより、矛先が急に変わる点を強調する。
contrastJapanese: round on は突然の攻撃。lay into は長く激しい非難。

meaning: Give someone an unwanted responsibility.
easyEnglish: Give someone an unwanted responsibility.
japanese: 望まない負担を、押しつける。
cue: A colleague was given a difficult task nobody wanted.
reply: They saddled him with the whole migration.
transferCue: Describe inheriting a problem.
transferReply: We were saddled with a system nobody understood.
nuance: The person goes between saddle and with. Usually passive, and always unwelcome.
contrast: Saddle with imposes a burden; entrust with gives a responsibility as a compliment.

exampleTranslations.They saddled him with the whole migratio: 彼は移行作業全体を、押しつけられました。
exampleTranslations.We were saddled with a system nobody und: 誰も理解していない仕組みを、押しつけられました。

nuanceJapanese: 相手は saddle と with のあいだに置く。受け身が多く、つねに歓迎されない負担を指す。
contrastJapanese: saddle with は重荷を押しつける。entrust with は信頼して任せること。

meaning: Increase the size of an operation.
easyEnglish: Increase the size of an operation.
japanese: 規模を、大きくする。
cue: A trial worked and now needs to grow.
reply: The pilot worked, so we'll scale it up.
transferCue: Describe growth limits.
transferReply: The method doesn't scale up beyond fifty users.
nuance: Separable: scale it up, or intransitive. Scale down is the opposite.
contrast: Scale up grows the whole operation; ramp up increases output within it.

試験導入がうまくいったので、規模を広げます。
exampleTranslations.The method doesn't scale up beyond fifty: その方法は、50人を超えると通用しません。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：scale it up。自動詞としても使う。反対は scale down。
contrastJapanese: scale up は事業の規模を広げる。ramp up はその中で産出を増やす。

meaning: Frighten someone away so they do not come or take part.
easyEnglish: Frighten someone away so they do not come or take part.
japanese: 怖がらせて、寄りつかなくさせる。
cue: A high price discouraged customers.
reply: The deposit scared off half the applicants.
transferCue: Describe birds in a garden.
transferReply: The cat scares off every bird in the garden.
nuance: Separable: scare them off. The cause is the subject, and the effect is usually unintended.
contrast: Scare off frightens people away; put off discourages them without fear.

exampleTranslations.The deposit scared off half the applican: その保証金で、応募者の半分が離れました。
exampleTranslations.The cat scares off every bird in the gar: あの猫が、庭の鳥を全部追い払ってしまいます。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：scare them off。主語は原因で、結果は意図しない場合が多い。
contrastJapanese: scare off は怖がらせて遠ざける。put off は恐怖なしに気をそぐ。

meaning: Remove unwanted things before they get through.
easyEnglish: Remove unwanted things before they get through.
japanese: 通す前に、不要なものを除く。
cue: A filter removes irrelevant applications.
reply: The first stage screens out incomplete forms.
transferCue: Describe reducing noise.
transferReply: Good headphones screen out the engine noise.
nuance: Separable: screen them out. Used for applications, noise and light.
contrast: Screen out filters before entry; weed out removes after examining each one.

exampleTranslations.The first stage screens out incomplete f: 第一段階で、記入漏れのある書類を除きます。
exampleTranslations.Good headphones screen out the engine no: よいヘッドホンは、エンジン音を遮ってくれます。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：screen them out。応募書類にも、騒音や光にも使う。
contrastJapanese: screen out は入る前にふるいにかける。weed out は個別に見て取り除く。

meaning: Close an area completely so nobody can enter.
easyEnglish: Close an area completely so nobody can enter.
japanese: 完全に封鎖して、出入りできなくする。
cue: Part of a building has been closed after damage.
reply: They sealed off the corridor after the leak.
transferCue: Describe a police operation.
transferReply: Officers sealed off both ends of the street.
nuance: Separable: seal it off. Stronger than close off: nothing gets in or out.
contrast: Seal off closes completely; cordon off marks a boundary people should not cross.

exampleTranslations.They sealed off the corridor after the l: 水漏れのあと、その廊下は封鎖されました。
exampleTranslations.Officers sealed off both ends of the str: 警官が、通りの両端を封鎖しました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：seal it off。close off より強く、出入りが完全に絶たれる。
contrastJapanese: seal off は完全に封鎖する。cordon off は越えてはならない境界を示す。

meaning: Continue until the end of a period.
easyEnglish: Continue until the end of a period.
japanese: その期間を、最後まで務め上げる。
cue: Someone is leaving but will finish the year.
reply: She'll see out the contract and then move.
transferCue: Describe staying through a difficult season.
transferReply: They saw out the winter on reduced hours.
nuance: Separable: see it out. See is irregular: saw, seen. See someone out means showing them to the door.
contrast: See out finishes a fixed period; stick it out emphasises enduring discomfort.

exampleTranslations.She'll see out the contract and then mov: 彼女は契約を全うしてから、移ります。
exampleTranslations.They saw out the winter on reduced hours: 彼らは時短で、冬を乗り切りました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：see it out。see は不規則変化で saw、seen。see someone out なら「見送る」の意味。
contrastJapanese: see out は決まった期間を務め上げる。stick it out はつらさに耐えることを強調する。

meaning: Look for something specific until you find it.
easyEnglish: Look for something specific until you find it.
japanese: 特定のものを、探し求める。
cue: You want a particular kind of specialist.
reply: It's worth seeking out a proper specialist.
transferCue: Describe travelling for food.
transferReply: He seeks out the best bakery in every town.
nuance: Separable: seek them out. Seek is irregular: sought. More deliberate than simply look for.
contrast: Seek out pursues something specific; cast around searches with no clear lead.

exampleTranslations.It's worth seeking out a proper speciali: きちんとした専門家を、探し出す価値はあります。
exampleTranslations.He seeks out the best bakery in every to: 彼はどの町でも、いちばんのパン屋を探し出します。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：seek them out。seek は不規則変化で sought。単なる look for より意図的。
contrastJapanese: seek out は特定のものを追う。cast around は当てもなく探す。

meaning: Take hold of something eagerly and make use of it.
easyEnglish: Take hold of something eagerly and make use of it.
japanese: すかさず飛びついて、利用する。
cue: A small error was used to attack a whole argument.
reply: Critics seized on the one wrong figure.
transferCue: Describe using a good idea quickly.
transferReply: She seized on the suggestion and built it out.
nuance: Inseparable; upon is the formal variant. It can be opportunistic or genuinely enthusiastic.
contrast: Seize on takes up an opportunity; pounce on stresses speed and often criticism.

批判する側は、間違った数字ひとつに飛びつきました。
exampleTranslations.She seized on the suggestion and built i: 彼女はその提案にすぐ飛びつき、形にしました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できず、upon は改まった形。打算的にも、純粋な熱意にも使える。
contrastJapanese: seize on は機会を捉える。pounce on は素早さと、多くは批判を強調する。

meaning: Post something, or order a player to leave the field.
easyEnglish: Post something, or order a player to leave the field.
japanese: 郵送する。また、選手を退場させる。
cue: An application must be posted today.
reply: I'll send off the forms this afternoon.
transferCue: Describe a football match.
transferReply: The referee sent him off in the first half.
nuance: Separable: send it off. Send is irregular: sent. The sport sense is British.
contrast: Send off posts something; send out distributes it to many people.

午後に、書類を郵送します。
exampleTranslations.The referee sent him off in the first ha: 前半で、審判が彼を退場させました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：send it off。send は不規則変化で sent。スポーツの意味はイギリス英語。
contrastJapanese: send off は郵送する。send out は多数に配る。

meaning: Present food, or offer something for people to receive.
easyEnglish: Present food, or offer something for people to receive.
japanese: 料理を出す。また、提供する。
cue: Dinner is ready for guests.
reply: I'll serve up as soon as they arrive.
transferCue: Describe a television schedule critically.
transferReply: They serve up the same format every year.
nuance: Separable: serve it up. Figuratively it can be critical, implying something unoriginal.
contrast: Serve up presents something; dish up is limited to putting food on plates.

到着したら、すぐ盛りつけて出します。
exampleTranslations.They serve up the same format every year: 毎年、同じ形式を出してくるだけです。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：serve it up。比喩的には、目新しさのなさへの批判になることがある。
contrastJapanese: serve up は広く提供する。dish up は料理を皿に盛ることに限られる。

meaning: Compare one thing with another, or make someone oppose another.
easyEnglish: Compare one thing with another, or make someone oppose another.
japanese: 引き比べる。また、対立させる。
cue: A cost should be judged next to a benefit.
reply: Set against the savings, the fee looks small.
transferCue: Describe a divisive dispute.
transferReply: The argument set neighbour against neighbour.
nuance: Set is irregular and unchanged: set. Two senses: weighing a comparison, and creating opposition.
contrast: Set against weighs two things; play off manipulates two parties against each other.

exampleTranslations.Set against the savings, the fee looks s: 節約分と比べれば、その手数料は小さく見えます。
exampleTranslations.The argument set neighbour against neigh: あの争いは、隣人同士を対立させました。

nuanceJapanese: set は不規則変化で形が変わらない。「比較する」と「対立させる」の2つの意味がある。
contrastJapanese: set against は二者を比べる。play off は二者を操って争わせる。

meaning: Write something officially, or put something on a surface.
easyEnglish: Write something officially, or put something on a surface.
japanese: 正式に書き記す。また、置く。
cue: A rule needs to exist in writing.
reply: The procedure is set down in the handbook.
transferCue: Describe putting something heavy down.
transferReply: He set the box down carefully.
nuance: Separable: set it down. Set is unchanged in the past. Often passive when about rules.
contrast: Set down records something formally; jot down is a quick informal note.

exampleTranslations.The procedure is set down in the handboo: その手順は、手引きに明記されています。
彼は箱を、そっと置きました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：set it down。set の過去形は同形。規則については受け身が多い。
contrastJapanese: set down は正式に記す。jot down は手早いメモ。

meaning: Begin and seem likely to continue.
easyEnglish: Begin and seem likely to continue.
japanese: 始まって、しばらく続きそうである。
cue: Bad weather has arrived for the season.
reply: The rain has set in for the week.
transferCue: Describe a mood in a team.
transferReply: A kind of weariness set in after March.
nuance: Intransitive, and almost always about something unwelcome: rain, winter, decay, doubt.
contrast: Set in is an unwelcome state taking hold; take root is about ideas becoming established.

今週いっぱい、雨が続きそうです。
3月を過ぎて、一種の疲れが居座りました。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞で、ほぼつねに歓迎されないものに使う。雨、冬、腐敗、疑念など。
contrastJapanese: set in は好ましくない状態が居座る。take root は考えが定着すること。

meaning: Become comfortable in a new place or routine.
easyEnglish: Become comfortable in a new place or routine.
japanese: 新しい場所や生活に、なじんでくる。
cue: A colleague has been in a new role for a month.
reply: She's settling into the job nicely.
transferCue: Describe moving house.
transferReply: It took us a month to settle into the flat.
nuance: Inseparable. Settle in without an object means the same, and settle down is about calming.
contrast: Settle into adjusts to a place or routine; settle for accepts something less than you wanted.

彼女は新しい仕事に、うまくなじんできています。
exampleTranslations.It took us a month to settle into the fl: その部屋に慣れるまで、1か月かかりました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない。目的語なしの settle in も同じ意味で、settle down は落ち着くこと。
contrastJapanese: settle into は場所や生活に慣れる。settle for は妥協して受け入れる。

meaning: Arrange something so the result is certain.
easyEnglish: Arrange something so the result is certain.
japanese: 手を打って、結果を確実にする。
cue: A deal is effectively already decided.
reply: They had the contract sewn up before we bid.
transferCue: Describe securing a result early.
transferReply: Two wins sewed up the title.
nuance: Separable: sew it up. Sew is irregular: sewed, sewn. Often passive: have it sewn up.
contrast: Sew up makes an outcome certain; nail down settles a specific detail.

exampleTranslations.They had the contract sewn up before we: こちらが入札する前に、契約は固まっていました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：sew it up。sew は不規則変化で sewed、sewn。have it sewn up の受け身が多い。
contrastJapanese: sew up は結果を確定させる。nail down は個々の細部を決める。

meaning: Divide something among a group.
easyEnglish: Divide something among a group.
japanese: みんなに分け与える。
cue: There is food left after an event.
reply: Let's share out what's left.
transferCue: Describe dividing work.
transferReply: The tasks were shared out evenly.
nuance: Separable: share it out. The out adds the sense of distributing to each person.
contrast: Share out distributes to a group; split the difference settles between two figures.

残ったぶんを、みんなで分けましょう。
作業は、均等に分けられました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：share it out。out が加わることで、各人に配る意味になる。
contrastJapanese: share out は集団に分配する。split the difference は二つの数字の間を取ること。

meaning: Reduce an amount by a small margin.
easyEnglish: Reduce an amount by a small margin.
japanese: わずかに削って、減らす。
cue: A small improvement reduced a journey time.
reply: The new route shaves off ten minutes.
transferCue: Describe cutting a cost slightly.
transferReply: We shaved off two per cent by ordering early.
nuance: Separable: shave it off. Used for time, cost and weight, always by a small amount.
contrast: Shave off trims a small amount; slash implies a large sudden cut.

新しい経路で、10分短縮できます。
exampleTranslations.We shaved off two per cent by ordering e: 早めに発注して、2パーセント削りました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：shave it off。時間や費用、重さについて、わずかな削減に使う。
contrastJapanese: shave off はわずかに削る。slash は大幅に切り込むこと。

meaning: Be clearly noticeable despite everything else.
easyEnglish: Be clearly noticeable despite everything else.
japanese: ほかに紛れず、はっきり伝わってくる。
cue: A nervous performance still showed talent.
reply: Her ability shone through despite the nerves.
transferCue: Describe a warmly written letter.
transferReply: His kindness shines through every paragraph.
nuance: Intransitive. Shine is irregular: shone. The quality is the subject, and it is always positive.
contrast: Shine through shows a quality despite obstacles; stand out is simply being noticeable.

exampleTranslations.Her ability shone through despite the ne: 緊張していても、彼女の力量ははっきり伝わりました。
exampleTranslations.His kindness shines through every paragr: 彼の優しさが、どの段落からも伝わってきます。

nuanceJapanese: 自動詞。shine は不規則変化で shone。主語は長所のほうで、つねに肯定的。
contrastJapanese: shine through は障害があっても長所が伝わる。stand out は単に目立つこと。

meaning: Reject an idea firmly and quickly.
easyEnglish: Reject an idea firmly and quickly.
japanese: 提案を、即座に退ける。
cue: A suggestion was dismissed immediately.
reply: They shot down the idea in about a minute.
transferCue: Ask for a fair hearing.
transferReply: Let me finish before you shoot it down.
nuance: Separable: shoot it down. Shoot is irregular: shot. It implies dismissal without real consideration.
contrast: Shoot down rejects an idea outright; pick holes in criticises it point by point.

exampleTranslations.They shot down the idea in about a minut: 1分ほどで、その案は退けられました。
退ける前に、最後まで言わせてください。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：shoot it down。shoot は不規則変化で shot。十分な検討なしの却下を含意する。
contrastJapanese: shoot down は即座に却下する。pick holes in は一つずつあらを探す。

meaning: Stop someone being heard by shouting louder.
easyEnglish: Stop someone being heard by shouting louder.
japanese: 大声でかき消して、発言させない。
cue: A speaker could not be heard at a public meeting.
reply: The speaker was shouted down.
transferCue: Describe protecting a quiet voice.
transferReply: Don't let anyone be shouted down here.
nuance: Separable: shout them down. Often passive, and always disapproving of the shouters.
contrast: Shout down silences a speaker; drown out is about sound covering sound.

その発言者は、怒号にかき消されました。
ここでは、誰の声もかき消させないでください。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：shout them down。受け身が多く、叫んだ側への批判をつねに含む。
contrastJapanese: shout down は発言を封じる。drown out は音が音をかき消すこと。

meaning: Avoid something because you find it unpleasant.
easyEnglish: Avoid something because you find it unpleasant.
japanese: 嫌で、尻込みして避ける。
cue: A leader did not avoid a difficult decision.
reply: She doesn't shrink from an unpopular choice.
transferCue: Describe avoiding confrontation.
transferReply: He shrinks from any kind of argument.
nuance: Inseparable and slightly formal. Shrink is irregular: shrank, shrunk. Often in the negative as praise.
contrast: Shrink from avoids out of distaste; fight shy of avoids out of reluctance or caution.

exampleTranslations.She doesn't shrink from an unpopular cho: 彼女は、支持されない決断からも逃げません。
彼はどんな口論からも、尻込みします。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できない、やや改まった表現。shrink は不規則変化で shrank、shrunk。否定形でほめることが多い。
contrastJapanese: shrink from は嫌悪から避ける。fight shy of は気後れや慎重さから避ける。

meaning: Keep someone or something in a place away from others.
easyEnglish: Keep someone or something in a place away from others.
japanese: 人目につかない場所に、しまい込む。
cue: Valuable items are kept in storage.
reply: The archive is shut away in the basement.
transferCue: Describe someone working in isolation.
transferReply: He shuts himself away when he's writing.
nuance: Separable: shut it away. Shut is irregular and unchanged. Reflexive for people who isolate themselves.
contrast: Shut away stores out of sight; lock away adds the idea of security.

exampleTranslations.The archive is shut away in the basement: その資料は、地下にしまい込まれています。
彼は執筆中、こもりきりになります。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：shut it away。shut は不規則変化で形が変わらない。人がこもる場合は再帰代名詞を使う。
contrastJapanese: shut away は人目から隠す。lock away は施錠して安全に保つ含みが加わる。

meaning: Choose one person or thing from a group for special attention.
easyEnglish: Choose one person or thing from a group for special attention.
japanese: 一人だけを、取り立てて扱う。
cue: One team was praised by name in a report.
reply: The report singled out the support team.
transferCue: Object to unfair attention.
transferReply: It's unfair to single out one person.
nuance: Separable: single them out. Neutral in itself; the context makes it praise or blame.
contrast: Single out picks one from many; pick on repeatedly targets the same person unfairly.

その報告書は、サポートチームを名指しで評価しました。
一人だけを取り上げるのは、公平ではありません。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：single them out。それ自体は中立で、文脈で称賛にも批判にもなる。
contrastJapanese: single out は多数から一つ選ぶ。pick on は同じ人を繰り返し不当に狙う。

meaning: Attend something as an observer.
easyEnglish: Attend something as an observer.
japanese: 参加者ではなく、聴講者として同席する。
cue: You want to observe a meeting without joining it.
reply: May I sit in on the review tomorrow?
transferCue: Describe training a new colleague.
transferReply: She sat in on three calls before taking her own.
nuance: Inseparable, with both in and on. Sit is irregular: sat. It means observing, not participating.
contrast: Sit in on observes a meeting; take part in means actively contributing.

exampleTranslations.May I sit in on the review tomorrow?: 明日の検討会に、聴講として同席してもよいですか。
exampleTranslations.She sat in on three calls before taking: 彼女は自分で対応する前に、3件の通話に同席しました。

nuanceJapanese: in と on の両方を伴い、分離できない。sit は不規則変化で sat。参加ではなく傍聴を意味する。
contrastJapanese: sit in on は傍聴する。take part in は積極的に参加する。

meaning: Not take part in something, or wait until it ends.
easyEnglish: Not take part in something, or wait until it ends.
japanese: 参加せずにいる。また、終わるまで待つ。
cue: You have an injury before a match.
reply: I'll sit this one out and play next week.
transferCue: Describe waiting through bad weather.
transferReply: We sat out the storm in a café.
nuance: Separable: sit it out. Sit is irregular: sat. Two senses: declining to join, and waiting something out.
contrast: Sit out declines to take part; opt out formally withdraws from a scheme.

exampleTranslations.I'll sit this one out and play next week: 今回は見送って、来週出ます。
カフェで、嵐が過ぎるのを待ちました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：sit it out。sit は不規則変化で sat。「参加しない」と「やり過ごす」の2つの意味がある。
contrastJapanese: sit out は参加を見送る。opt out は制度から正式に離脱する。

meaning: Take the best part, or take money dishonestly.
easyEnglish: Take the best part, or take money dishonestly.
japanese: 上澄みを取る。また、不正に抜き取る。
cue: A scheme takes the strongest candidates first.
reply: The programme skims off the top applicants.
transferCue: Describe an investigation finding.
transferReply: Someone had been skimming off small amounts.
nuance: Separable: skim it off. The dishonest sense is common in reports of fraud.
contrast: Skim off takes the best or takes covertly; cream off is limited to taking the best.

exampleTranslations.The programme skims off the top applican: その制度は、上位の応募者を先に取っていきます。
exampleTranslations.Someone had been skimming off small amou: 少額を抜き取っていた人がいました。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：skim it off。不正に抜き取る意味は、不正報道でよく使う。
